text: When you see this sign, you should –
options: Take a break, rest area ahead.
Drive carefully and watch out for traffic entering from a side-road intersection ahead.
Take care, trucks crossing the road ahead.

text: You want to turn left at this intersection. There is an edge line that continues through the intersection. Are you permitted to turn here?
options: Yes, you can cross an edge line to turn into or out of a street.
No, not under any circumstances.
Yes, only if you are in a taxi, hire car, bus or you live in that street.
explanation: Yes, you can cross an edge line to turn into or out of a street. This matters because lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: When you see children on or near the road -
options: You should slow down and be more careful because they may move suddenly.
You should reduce your speed by 5 km/h.
You should ignore them and pay attention to the rear vision mirror.
explanation: You should slow down and be more careful because they may move suddenly. It is safer because children can be unpredictable and may step out without warning.

text: A section of road is marked with double unbroken dividing lines as in the diagram. When is a vehicle allowed to cross these lines?
options: To overtake a slow vehicle ahead.
Only to enter or leave a street or driveway, or to pass a cyclist.
When there is no traffic coming the other way.

text: You should be particularly careful at this intersection because -
options: The building blocks a good view of the side street.
Intersections cause crashes.
It looks a bit tricky.
explanation: The building blocks a good view of the side street. It helps because limited sight lines mean you need extra caution to avoid conflicts.

text: To ensure prescription drugs will not affect your ability to ride a motorcycle you should -
options: Tell your doctor you ride a motorcycle, check with your pharmacist and read the label on the drugs.
Not ride at all while taking any medication.
Not take the medication if you want to ride.

text: Can a P1 or P2 provisional driver legally instruct a learner driver?
options: No.
Yes, provided the provisional driver has held a P2 licence for more than 6 months.
Yes, provided L and P1 or P2 plates are displayed.
explanation: No. It helps because licensing rules exist to build experience before taking on more responsibility.

text: Protective clothing should be -
options: Comfortable without being loose.
Loose to allow air flow to keep you cool in summer.
Very tight so they won't move if you fall off your bike.

text: Even if you feel unaffected after drinking alcohol, you should -
options: Spend more time than usual looking in the mirrors.
Be aware that your abilities are decreased.
Drive, but avoid using busy roads.

text: When being overtaken by another vehicle what should you do to help?
options: Keep left and allow plenty of room to let the other vehicle back in.
Brake quickly to let the other vehicle overtake.
Move to the left and stop.
explanation: Keep left and allow plenty of room to let the other vehicle back in. This matters because overtake only when the road is clear and it is safe for all traffic.

text: Many people crash within the first few years of driving. What is the best way of learning to drive on your own without crashing?
options: Drive as much as you can with friends on the way to parties.
Start driving in daylight where it is not too busy and only drive in busier traffic as your driving gets better.
Drive in every kind of traffic situation as soon as you get your licence. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 106 of 121

text: Wearing the right protective clothing when riding can -
options: Greatly reduce injury in the event of a crash.
Make no difference to you when you ride.
Make you very hot and reduce your ability to ride.

text: When turning left at a roundabout you should enter and leave the roundabout -
options: In the left lane.
In the lane with least traffic.
In the right lane.

text: If a traffic controller displays a stop sign you must -
options: Stop your vehicle and follow the directions of the traffic controller.
Slow your vehicle down and continue through the road works zone.
Stop your vehicle and then proceed if you think it is safe.

text: At night, when you approach an oncoming vehicle, you should -
options: Carefully watch the vehicle by looking directly at its headlights.
Not look at its headlights, but keep left and watch the left of the road.
Put your lights on high beam, to make your vehicle more easily seen.

text: Which movements shown in the diagram can legally be made by the driver of the purple car?
options: O, P and Q.
O and P only.
P only.

text: You want to park your vehicle for a short time. It is night time. You should -
options: Pick a visible position or leave the parking lights on.
Park on the footpath.
Leave your headlights on high beam.

text: When riding on a wet road, what is usually the most slippery part?
options: The right wheel track.
The left wheel track.
The centre of the lane and painted road markings.

text: Driving faster than the maximum speed limit is -
options: Never legally permitted.
Permitted only when passing another vehicle.
Only permitted when other vehicles are going faster than the speed limit.
explanation: Never legally permitted. It helps because higher speeds increase stopping distance and crash severity.

text: To make a normal stop, you should use -
options: The front brake only.
Both front and rear brakes.
The rear brake only.

text: RUH8 When it is very foggy during the day or night and your vehicle has no fog lights, you should -
options: Slow down and use your low beam headlights and hazard warning lights to make your vehicle seen.
Put on your high beam lights.
Follow closer to other vehicles.
explanation: Slow down and use your low beam headlights and hazard warning lights to make your vehicle seen. This matters because staying alert and scanning early gives you time to react.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Merging traffic, give way to your right.
Form one lane of traffic.
Road narrows ahead, slow down and prepare for a change in traffic conditions. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 80 of 121

text: You are about to make a right hand turn at this intersection. You have the green light. You hear a siren and then see that a fire truck will soon overtake you. You should -
options: Stop and let the fire truck overtake you.
Continue and make the turn because you have the right of way.
Speed up to beat the fire truck.
explanation: Stop and let the fire truck overtake you. This matters because overtake only when the road is clear and it is safe for all traffic.

text: If you are a new driver and first start to drive at night you should -
options: Drive mainly on streets that you know well.
Drive mainly in unfamiliar streets.
Drive long distances to improve your concentration.
explanation: Drive mainly on streets that you know well. That reduces risk since reduced visibility means hazards appear later and take longer to react to.

text: When approaching a railway level crossing displaying this sign, you must -
options: Slow down, look both ways for trains and be prepared to stop if necessary.
Increase your speed to avoid any approaching trains.
Continue across at normal speed, do not slow down.
explanation: Slow down, look both ways for trains and be prepared to stop if necessary. This matters because trains cannot stop quickly, so you only proceed when the crossing is clear.

text: You are driving a vehicle that only has a seat belt for the driver. To reduce the danger of being in a vehicle without a seat belt, where is the best place for passengers to sit?
options: In the back seat.
In the front seat.
In the front seat sharing your seat belt.
explanation: In the back seat. That reduces risk since restraints keep occupants in place and reduce injury in a crash.

text: When driving in wet weather, you should -
options: Watch out for pedestrians, who may hurry and take risks.
Drive in the middle of the road to avoid splashing pedestrians on the footpath.
Stop and help aged pedestrians across the road.
explanation: Watch out for pedestrians, who may hurry and take risks. It is safer because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: When reversing, you should -
options: Take care and never reverse for a greater distance and time than is necessary.
Unbuckle your seat belt so you can reverse as quickly as possible.
Sound your horn to warn other drivers.
explanation: Take care and never reverse for a greater distance and time than is necessary. It helps because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: You are driving in a 60 km/h zone, with only one lane for traffic in your direction. You see a bus ahead (with this sign displayed on the rear) signaling its intention to pull out from a bus stop, you should -
options: Continue at your normal speed as the bus does not have priority.
Slow down, and give way to the bus as it has priority.
Sound your horn to stop the bus from pulling out.

text: Every time before you ride you should check -
options: That the headlight and stop light are working.
That your motorcycle is clean.
Your street directory.

text: If you get sleepy while driving, it is best to -
options: Stop, rest, and change drivers if possible.
Turn on the radio very loud.
Turn on the air conditioning or open the windows.
explanation: Stop, rest, and change drivers if possible. It is safer because fatigue reduces attention and reaction time.

text: Are you required to carry your driver’s licence with you every time you drive?
options: No, being licensed is enough.
Yes.
No, it is only needed on long trips.

text: Which of the following attitudes is most likely to make you a safer driver?
options: When I drive, I have the main responsibility for my safety and the safety of other road users.
Crashing or not crashing is a matter of luck.
It is up to other drivers to avoid crashing into me. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 105 of 121

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Turn around and go back, you are going the wrong way.
Sharp bend to the right ahead, slow down and drive carefully.
No right turn allowed.

text: You drive up to an intersection with a stop sign in the car marked A and you wish to turn right. The car marked B facing you also has a stop sign and is indicating to turn left. Who can go first?
options: Car B.
Car A.
Whoever arrives at the intersection first.
explanation: Car B. This matters because right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: If a STOP or GIVE WAY sign has been knocked down, for example, as the result of an accident, does the line marked across the road have any meaning?
options: No, you only need to give way to the vehicle on your right.
Yes, it has the same meaning as the sign itself.
No, but you must give way if turning.

text: You drive into a transit lane where the T2 rule applies. You have one passenger plus yourself. Are you permitted to remain in the transit lane?
options: Yes, you have two people in your car so you can drive in this lane.
No, because you only have one passenger you must move out of the transit lane immediately.
Yes, you can remain in the transit lane, but only if you are turning left in 250 metres.
explanation: Yes, you have two people in your car so you can drive in this lane. That reduces risk since special lanes keep high-occupancy or public transport moving, and misuse disrupts flow.

text: How old must you be to obtain a learner rider licence?
options: 15 years of age.
16 years and 3 months of age.
16 years of age.

text: Temporary traffic lights at road works -
options: Must be obeyed.
Apply to road works vehicles only.
Are installed to warn motorists of construction works.
explanation: Must be obeyed. This matters because lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: If you are convicted of dangerous driving -
options: You could lose your licence and may be sent to prison.
You could be given demerit points only.
You could only be fined and given demerit points.

text: If you are overtaking a motorcycle you should -
options: Sound your horn flash your lights before you overtake.
Overtake as close as possible, to avoid going fully into the oncoming lane.
Give plenty of room and overtake only when safe.

text: When carrying a pillion passenger, the passenger should sit -
options: Behind and as close as possible to the rider.
Behind and as far from the rider as possible.
In front of and as close to the rider as possible.

text: Before beginning to overtake another vehicle, you should -
options: Sound your horn, move out and overtake.
Check to see it is safe, change gear if necessary, and signal your intention before moving out.
Signal and slow down so you will have more room to overtake.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Workers ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop.
Children's playground ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop.
Do not litter.
explanation: Workers ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop. That reduces risk since signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: What type of Class R motorcycle licence is required to legally lane filter?
options: Any type of Class R licence.
Full, open unrestricted Class R licence.
Any type of Class R licence other than a Learner Licence.

text: You must give way to pedestrians if there is a risk of hitting them. When driving in poor light, you should -
options: Look more carefully for pedestrians because they are hard to see.
Keep your headlights on high beam all the time.
Always drive in the right hand lane so you can be away from pedestrians.
explanation: Look more carefully for pedestrians because they are hard to see. It is safer because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: An important part of observation is -
options: Constantly performing head checks.
Keeping your chin up and look straight at all times.
Scanning.

text: If you hear the siren of an emergency vehicle, you must -
options: Increase your speed to avoid the vehicle.
Flash your headlights to warn other drivers.
Take whatever action is necessary (with safety) to make way for the emergency vehicle.

text: You give a friend and her 12 year old son a lift. Your friend sits in the front and her son gets in the back. The boy does not put his seat belt on. By law, who has to make sure the child wears his seat belt?
options: Your friend does because she is the parent.
The child does because it is always the passenger's responsibility.
You do, because you are the driver.

text: In what part of the lane should you ride when being passed by on-coming vehicles?
options: No special part of your lane.
As close to the centre line as possible.
The centre or left of your lane.

text: How should you overtake a pedal cyclist?
options: The same as you would another car, with safety.
Drive as close as possible to the cyclist so he or she will move over and let you pass.
Sound your horn to warn the cyclist to get off the road.
explanation: The same as you would another car, with safety. It is safer because cyclists are vulnerable, and consistent rules keep their movements predictable.

text: When driving in wet weather, your vehicle will -
options: Take longer and further to stop, so slow down.
Stop in the same distance as on a dry road.
Handle better, so you can go faster.
explanation: Take longer and further to stop, so slow down. That reduces risk since wet roads reduce grip and increase stopping distance.

text: A pillion passenger should hold on to -
options: The rider's waist, hips or passenger's grab rail.
The rider's helmet.
The rider's arms.

text: In what part of the lane should you ride when being passed by on-coming vehicles?
options: The centre or left of your lane.
No special part of your lane.
As close to the centre line as possible.

text: If you are involved in an accident where your vehicle needs to be towed away and the Police does not attend the crash scene, you -
options: Must report the accident to the Police Station nearest to where the accident happened within 24 hours.
Do not need to report the accident to the Police.
Only need to report the accident to the Police if someone was injured.
explanation: Must report the accident to the Police Station nearest to where the accident happened within 24 hours. It is safer because getting help quickly reduces harm and keeps the scene safe.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: There is a hump (sudden slope up and down) in the road ahead, slow down.
There is a tunnel ahead, turn on your headlights.
The road ahead is closed, go back.

text: Wearing a helmet visor or goggles when riding will -
options: Protect your eyes from the wind, dust, rain, insects or stones thrown up by other vehicles.
Reduce your vision and should only be worn in the rain.
Not make much difference to your riding on a fine day when there is no wind.

text: You drive up to a corner where you see some loose gravel on the road. You should -
options: Slow down.
Check the mirrors and change lanes.
Speed up and drive over the gravel as quickly as possible.
explanation: Slow down. It is safer because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: What are you required to do if you develop a serious medical condition that could affect your driving?
options: Once you become aware of the condition you must notify the RTA.
Hand your licence in at the nearest police station.
Tell your doctor and let him or her notify the RTA.
explanation: Once you become aware of the condition you must notify the RTA. That reduces risk since predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: You must not drive faster than 100 km/h.
You must drive faster than 100 km/h.
The sign applies to truck drivers only, cars can travel at any speed.
explanation: You must not drive faster than 100 km/h. This matters because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: In a turn you should tell a pillion passenger to -
options: Lean in the opposite direction from the turn.
Stay upright.
Lean in the same direction as the rider.

text: If turning at an intersection are you required to give way to pedestrians?
options: Yes, a driver turning right or left must give way to pedestrians, if there is a danger of a collision
Yes, only if turning left.
Yes, only if turning right.
explanation: Yes, a driver turning right or left must give way to pedestrians, if there is a danger of a collision. This matters because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: Head checks are what drivers and riders do to -
options: See what is in their blind spots.
See what is behind them.
See what is to the front side of them.
explanation: See what is in their blind spots. A head check is the only way to see blind spots the mirrors miss.

text: The motorcyclist wants to travel straight ahead through this roundabout. The rider should watch out for the marked car because the car -
options: Could be going too fast.
May stop suddenly.
May be leaving the roundabout.

text: The diagram shows a marked pedestrian crossing at an intersection. There is also a STOP sign at the intersection. You have already stopped for a pedestrian. Must you stop again at the STOP line?
options: Yes, at all times.
Yes, if there is traffic on your right only.
No, if the intersection is clear.
explanation: Yes, at all times. It helps because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: You should expect this sign, when -
options: A two lane bridge is ahead, slow down and drive carefully.
Freeway conditions are ahead, maximum speed is 100 km/h.
A divided road is ahead, prepare for a change in traffic conditions. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 79 of 121

text: It is night time and you are driving home from the movies. You are travelling in a line of vehicles. What size gap should you leave between your vehicle and the vehicles in front of you?
options: A gap of about 4 seconds as it is easy to misjudge distances at night.
A gap of about 2 seconds so you can watch the vehicles in front closely and see when they are stopping.
The same 3-second gap you would leave during the day.
explanation: A gap of about 4 seconds as it is easy to misjudge distances at night. This matters because reduced visibility means hazards appear later and take longer to react to.

text: To drive safely, you need to concentrate and be able to monitor everything that is happening on the road. To do this, you need to -
options: Turn all your attention only to the road ahead.
Continually scan the road, looking ahead, to the sides, checking side and rear mirrors and anticipate what may happen.
Ask other occupants in the vehicle to watch out for possible dangers.

text: You are driving your vehicle along a street and want to stop for a short time. Are you allowed to double park your vehicle (that is stand it on the road alongside a parked car)?
options: Yes, provided you stop for a short time only and turn on your hazard warning lights.
No, never.
Yes, provided you do not leave the vehicle.

text: You wish to turn left at this intersection and the traffic lights are green. What should you do?
options: Wait behind the stop line until there is room for you to enter the new road.
Move forward slowly, make the left turn and wait behind car A.
Enter the intersection and sound the horn.
explanation: Wait behind the stop line until there is room for you to enter the new road. It is safer because lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: You wish to go straight ahead on this roundabout with two lanes. Which lane may you use?
options: Right lane only.
Left lane only.
Either lane. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 27 of 121

text: You are approaching the crest (top of a hill) on a narrow road, the safest procedure is to -
options: Increase your speed and sound your horn.
Flash your headlights to warn oncoming traffic.
Keep to the left and slow down.

text: In order to provide the minimum safe passing distance for bicycle riders, are you permitted to cross single and double continuous lines?
options: no.
yes, always
yes, but you must have a clear view of any approaching traffic and it must be safe to do so.
explanation: no. That reduces risk since cyclists are vulnerable, and consistent rules keep their movements predictable.

text: Alcohol is a depressant. This means -
options: It slows down how quickly your brain works.
It speeds your brain up so you can work better.
It makes you calm down and think more clearly.
explanation: It slows down how quickly your brain works. This matters because alcohol and drugs slow reactions and impair judgment.

text: A vehicle ahead of you has stopped at a pedestrian crossing. You -
options: Must not overtake the stopped vehicle.
May overtake the vehicle provided no cars are coming the other way.
May overtake the vehicle if there are no pedestrians on the crossing.

text: You must give way to pedestrians on a marked pedestrian crossing -
options: If there is any danger of a collision.
When they are crossing from your right only.
When they are crossing from your left only.
explanation: If there is any danger of a collision. It helps because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: When learning to ride you should -
options: Start in quiet streets that you know well.
Ride in groups so that you are protected from cars.
Gain experience in complex traffic situations to build your skills quickly.

text: You want to turn right at an intersection and see this traffic light. You should -
options: Stay behind the stop line until the green arrow shows.
Move forward slowly.
Enter the intersection and wait for the green arrow.
explanation: Stay behind the stop line until the green arrow shows. That reduces risk since lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: A pillion passenger should hold on to -
options: The rider's waist, hips or passenger's handgrip.
The rider's arms.
The rider's helmet.

text: Which statement is correct?
options: Red light cameras take photographs of vehicles that cross intersections when the lights are yellow.
Red light cameras take photographs of vehicles that enter intersections when the lights are red.
Red light cameras take photographs of vehicles that speed through intersections.

text: You are in car marked Y and want to turn right using a median turning lane. A car marked O, coming towards you, is already in the median lane; it is slowing down and indicating. Are you permitted to enter and share the median turning lane?
options: Yes, but you must be prepared to slow down and stop.
No, if another car is already in the median turning lane you must not use it.
Yes, but only if you race the other car and get to the turning position first.
explanation: Yes, but you must be prepared to slow down and stop. It is safer because lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: If you find cracks or loose padding in your helmet you should -
options: Have it repaired by an authorised person.
Use high speed duct tape to hold it together as it is waterproof.
Replace it.

text: If you see a sign indicating road repairs are going on, you should -
options: Slow down and watch for traffic controllers and instructions.
Stop immediately and wait for instructions.
Maintain the same speed.
explanation: Slow down and watch for traffic controllers and instructions. It helps because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: To ensure a helmet is in good condition you should -
options: Only purchase a new one. Never buy a second hand helmet.
Check to make sure it has not been dropped.
Only buy a helmet that someone else has tried out first.

text: If you are taking several medications and you want to drive, you should -
options: Ask your doctor if the combination of drugs will make it dangerous to drive.
Drive carefully around your local streets to see if you are affected.
Ask your passengers to let you know if you are not driving as well as you should.
explanation: Ask your doctor if the combination of drugs will make it dangerous to drive. It is safer because alcohol and drugs slow reactions and impair judgment.

text: If you are convicted of dangerous driving -
options: You could lose your licence and may be sent to prison.
You could only be fined and given demerit points.
You could be given demerit points only.
explanation: You could lose your licence and may be sent to prison. It helps because careless actions create unpredictable conflicts.

text: Before driving a motor vehicle or riding a motor cycle it is safest to -
options: Drink 1 middy (285 ml) of light (low alcohol) beer.
Drink 1 nip of spirits (30 ml or 1 oz).
Not drink any alcohol.

text: You are approaching a green light in vehicle A. An ambulance sounding its siren is approaching the same intersection and has a red light. You should -
options: Keep driving because you have the green light.
Pull over to the left before you reach the intersection.
Slow down and stop if necessary to prevent getting in its way. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 100 of 121

text: When riding on a single lane road, a motorcycle rider -
options: In the direction you wish to go.
At traffic coming from behind.
Down, so you can see the road immediately in front of you.

text: What should drivers do if they can’t leave the minimum safe passing distance for passing a cyclist?
options: Speed up and pass the cyclist as quickly as possible.
Slow down, be patient and wait until it is safe to pass.
Drivers should use their horn to make the cyclist move to one side.

text: You are riding the motorcycle shown, what would you need to do to be able to see the car?
options: Turn your head.
Look in the mirror.
Take off your helmet.
explanation: Turn your head. Mirrors have blind spots, so a head check confirms the car before you move.

text: You are travelling in the left lane and wish to turn right at the intersection. You move to the right lane and a driver behind sounds their horn at you. What have you done wrong?
options: Changed lanes unnecessarily.
Crossed an unbroken lane line.
Driven too slowly. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 45 of 121

text: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: You must give way to pedestrians if there is a danger of a collision.
Pedestrians must cross the road only at marked crossings and intersections.
You do not have to give way to adults crossing at children's crossings.
explanation: You must give way to pedestrians if there is a danger of a collision. This matters because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: What is the best way to avoid hitting other vehicles, people or animals when moving off from the kerb?
options: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before moving off from the kerb.
Have a good look around while you walk up to your car and then drive off as soon as you can.
Sound your horn before moving away from the kerb to warn people of your intentions.
explanation: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before moving off from the kerb. That reduces risk since animals are unpredictable and can enter the road suddenly.

text: If one or two of your wheels run off the edge of the roadway, you should -
options: Slow down gradually and ease back onto the road.
Slow down quickly by braking hard.
Increase your speed and drive back on the road.
explanation: Slow down gradually and ease back onto the road. This matters because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: Are you permitted to park on a median strip or traffic island?
options: No, not at any time.
Yes, in daylight hours.
Yes, but for no more than 30 minutes.
explanation: No, not at any time. This matters because parking safely and being visible prevents collisions and obstruction.

text: Following this vehicle too closely is unwise because -
options: Your engine will overheat.
Your brakes will overheat.
Your view ahead is reduced.

text: It is 4:30pm on a school day. You are driving at 60 km/h, the same speed as traffic around you. You approach this sign but the other cars do not slow down much. What should you do?
options: Slow down immediately to 40 km/h or less even though other drivers want to go faster.
Drive at the speed of the other drivers because it is safer to go with the flow of traffic than slow others up.
Stay at 60 km/h because it is nearly 5pm and the times on the school sign are only advisory.

text: When starting to overtake you see the dividing lines ahead change to double unbroken lines. What should you do?
options: Continue to overtake because you started when the line was broken.
Do not overtake because you are not permitted to overtake on double lines.
Keep overtaking and cut in front of the other car as soon as possible. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 113 of 121

text: Which sign painted on the road tells you there is a pedestrian crossing ahead?
options: B
C
A Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 49 of 121

text: You have a six year old child with you in your car. You have just parked so you can collect a prescription from the chemist. You should -
options: Take the child with you.
Leave the child in the car.
Ask an older person sitting nearby to watch the child.
explanation: Take the child with you. That reduces risk since children can be unpredictable and may step out without warning.

text: In addition to wearing a motorcycle helmet you should -
options: Wear a hair-net to help your helmet last longer.
Ensure that you always wear motorcycle specific clothing.
Make sure that you also wear sunglasses for additional protection.

text: The first thing you should do before overtaking is -
options: Make sure it is safe and the way is clear of oncoming traffic.
Sound your horn.
Increase your speed.
explanation: Make sure it is safe and the way is clear of oncoming traffic. It helps because overtake only when the road is clear and it is safe for all traffic.

text: At low speeds, if the front tyre goes flat what is the first thing you will notice?
options: The motorcycle will lean heavily to one side.
The motorcycle will tend to slide from side to side.
The steering will feel heavy.

text: The red car wants to turn right and exit the roundabout in the street indicated by an arrow. Is the car positioned in the correct lane to do this?
options: No, the car should enter the roundabout only from the right hand lane.
Yes, the car can make the turn only from this lane.
Yes, the car can make the turn from either the left hand or the right hand lane.
explanation: No, the car should enter the roundabout only from the right hand lane. It helps because roundabouts rely on lane discipline and giving way to avoid side impacts.

text: If elderly people or children are on a pedestrian crossing you will probably need to -
options: Wait extra time to allow them to cross safely.
Sound your horn to hurry them up.
Drive around them so you don't hold up traffic.

text: Babies under 6 months old must travel -
options: In the front seat using a seat belt.
In an approved baby restraint (e.g. baby capsule) attached to an anchorage point.
In the front seat with a parent.

text: You are in car marked A. You wish to overtake car marked B. You should -
options: Cross the unbroken single line and overtake.
Wait behind car B until it moves into the left lane.
Cross the line and overtake only if it is safe.

text: You want to turn right at an intersection and see this traffic light. You should –
options: Move forward slowly.
Stay behind the stop line until the green arrow shows.
Enter the intersection and wait for the green arrow. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 38 of 121

options: T-intersection ahead. If you are on the terminating road, you must give way to all vehicles approaching from your right or left.
Traffic lights ahead.
No through road ahead, slow down.

Unlikely to walk near the road and do not require your attention.
Less dangerous than sober pedestrians because they are more careful after drinking.
explanation: One of the most common groups involved in road accidents. It helps because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: You want to give a lift to a friend and his four month old baby. Before you do, you need to make sure -
options: You have enough seat belts for all the passengers, including the baby.
You have a baby restraint properly fitted to your vehicle.
Your driver's licence permits you to carry children under the age of twelve months. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 118 of 121

text: When driving in traffic lanes (as shown in the diagram), you may change your lane -
options: Only when it is safe to do so.
Without looking, provided you use your indicator
Provided you sound your horn to warn other drivers
explanation: Only when it is safe to do so. It helps because lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: Vehicle O is at a STOP sign -
options: Vehicle O must give way to vehicles P, Q and R.
Vehicle O must give way only to vehicle R.
All vehicles must give way to vehicle O.
explanation: Vehicle O must give way to vehicles P, Q and R. It is safer because giving way prevents conflicts with traffic that has priority.

text: When driving near children, playing or walking near the edge of the road, you should -
options: Blow your horn and continue at the same speed.
Drive close to the children so they will see you.
Slow down, and be ready to make a safe stop.

text: The best type of footwear when riding are -
options: Boots which provide ankle protection.
Trainers or Joggers.
Steel toe capped boots.

text: When approaching a marked pedestrian crossing and no pedestrians are in sight, you should -
options: Slow down and be ready to make a safe stop.
Come to a complete stop before the crossing.
Go faster, in case a pedestrian steps onto the crossing.
explanation: Slow down and be ready to make a safe stop. That reduces risk since pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: If you are taking any sort of medicine, you should -
options: Find out from your doctor or chemist whether the medicine or drug will affect your driving and act accordingly.
Only drive during the day after taking the medicine or drug.
Only drive a motor car not a heavy vehicle.

text: As you drive into an intersection, the lights turn to yellow. You should -
options: Continue through the intersection.
Accelerate as hard as you can.
Brake immediately to a stop.
explanation: Continue through the intersection. This matters because right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: The best type of footwear when riding are -
options: Boots which provide ankle protection.
Sand shoes or joggers.
Sandals with rubber soles and ankle straps as a minimum.

text: As you approach a set of traffic lights at an intersection, they change from green to yellow (amber). You must -
options: Stop before the lights, unless you are so close that sudden braking might cause an accident.
Drive through the intersection without accelerating.
Accelerate to clear the intersection before the lights change to red.
explanation: Stop before the lights, unless you are so close that sudden braking might cause an accident. This matters because stopping prevents you entering a conflict or hazard unexpectedly.

text: You must use your indicator lights when -
options: Changing lanes or turning left or right.
Approaching a curve.
Double parking.
explanation: Changing lanes or turning left or right. That reduces risk since lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: You are driving in busy traffic in a 60 km/h zone. You feel 60 km/h is a bit too fast for the conditions. What should you do?
options: Slow down to a speed that suits the conditions.
Keep up with the other traffic because it's probably safe if the sign says 60 km/h.
Turn off the busy street and wait for traffic to clear.
explanation: Slow down to a speed that suits the conditions. That reduces risk since higher speeds increase stopping distance and crash severity.

text: You approach an intersection showing a red light and the sign shown. You wish to turn left. You must -
options: Stop and turn left only if it is safe.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Slow down and turn left or right if it is safe.
explanation: Stop and turn left only if it is safe. This matters because stopping prevents you entering a conflict or hazard unexpectedly.

text: Before changing lanes you should -
options: Signal for at least two seconds and quickly change lanes.
Signal in plenty of time, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for other vehicles.
Speed up so you are going faster than the traffic in the other lane.

text: You wish to turn left here. The pedestrian lights are flashing red. You should -
options: Give way to pedestrians still crossing.
Move into the right hand lane.
Slowly move through the intersection turning left.
explanation: Give way to pedestrians still crossing. It is safer because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: You are riding along on a sealed road when you see sand on the road ahead. What should you do?
options: Slow down because it takes longer to stop on a slippery road surface.
Stay at the same speed.
Increase your speed.

text: On Thursday, Friday and Saturday nights, how many serious crashes involve alcohol?
options: About 50%.
About 30%.
About 10%.
explanation: About 50%. It helps because alcohol and drugs slow reactions and impair judgment.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: You must not turn to the right.
You may turn to the right.
You must give way to traffic on your right.

text: You are approaching the intersection shown, and an on-coming vehicle is signalling to turn right, you should -
options: Stop, and let the car turn right.
Move towards the left of your lane and prepare to take evasive action.
Proceed straight ahead at normal speed.

text: You must give way to pedestrians on a marked pedestrian crossing -
options: If there is any danger of a collision.
When they are crossing from your right only.
When they are crossing from your left only. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 48 of 121

text: The speed limit on this road is 100 km/h. When can you use the right lane?
options: Whenever you want to.
Only when overtaking or turning right.
When there is no other traffic around.

text: If you get sleepy while driving, out of the following, which is it best to do?
options: Stop, rest, and change drivers if possible.
Turn on the heater.
Turn on the radio very loud.

text: Where must L or P plates be displayed on a vehicle -
options: On the front and back of the exterior of the vehicle.
Anywhere including on the dashboard.
Anywhere inside the windows but only if they are not tinted.
explanation: On the front and back of the exterior of the vehicle. It is safer because clear plates warn other drivers so they can adjust and give space.

text: When driving on a multi-lane road with a speed limit of more than 80 km/h, which lane should you choose?
options: The left lane unless overtaking.
The right lane to avoid slow moving vehicles.
Either left or right lane.
explanation: The left lane unless overtaking. That reduces risk since higher speeds increase stopping distance and crash severity.

text: What should you do on approaching a railway level crossing displaying a STOP sign?
options: Stop, only if a train is at the crossing.
Slow down to 10 km/h, then proceed through the crossing.
Stop at all times and proceed when safe to do so. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 19 of 121

text: To reduce the effect of alcohol before driving or riding you should -
options: Drink black coffee.
Wait. The time depends on how much you have had to drink.
Have a glass of water.

text: If you find cracks or loose padding in your helmet you should -
options: Replace it.
Have it repaired by an authorised person.
Use high speed duct tape to hold it together as it is waterproof.

text: You are approaching the intersection shown, and an on-coming vehicle is signalling to turn right, you should -
options: Move towards the left of your lane and slow down.
Proceed straight ahead at normal speed.
Stop, and let the car turn right.
explanation: Move towards the left of your lane and slow down. This gives you space if the car turns across your path and buys reaction time.

text: Having a radar detector in your car is against the law -
options: Only if it is turned on.
If you purchased it after 1998.
No matter what your reason is. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 121 of 121

text: You are going to a party where everyone is drinking alcohol. What can you do to lower the risk of being in an alcohol related crash on the way home?
options: Get a taxi or other public transport there and back, or organise for someone to pick you up.
Take your car, try not to drink too much alcohol and then drive home.
Organise a lift home with someone from the party. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 9 of 121

text: Which movements shown in the diagram can legally be made by the driver of the purple car?
options: O and P only.
P only.
O, P and Q.
explanation: O and P only. That reduces risk since lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: To drive safely, you need to concentrate and be able to monitor everything that is happening on the road. To do this, you need to -
options: Continually scan the road, looking ahead, to the sides, checking side and rear mirrors and anticipate what may happen.
Turn all your attention only to the road ahead.
Ask other occupants in the vehicle to watch out for possible dangers.
explanation: Continually scan the road, looking ahead, to the sides, checking side and rear mirrors and anticipate what may happen. This matters because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: This intersection does not have any traffic lights or signs. You are in car A and want to turn right. When can you go?
options: Before the car going straight ahead has passed.
As soon as you get to the intersection.
After the car going straight ahead has passed.

text: When two lanes merge into one (as shown in the diagram), who should give way?
options: The vehicle which has to cross the lane line.
The faster vehicle.
The vehicle in the right-hand lane because it is overtaking.

text: You are at a busy intersection with slow moving traffic and want to go straight ahead. When the traffic lights change to green you should make sure that -
options: You do not block the intersection.
You have the car in the right gear.
You do not hold up the traffic behind you.
explanation: You do not block the intersection. That reduces risk since right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: If both vehicles P and O in the diagram are turning right, which vehicle is in the best position to turn left into the street marked 'X'?
options: Vehicle O.
Neither vehicle.
Vehicle P. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 16 of 121

text: Providing they are not breaking the speed limit, what is the maximum speed for learner drivers?
options: 80 km/h.
60 km/h.

text: You are in the car approaching the intersection shown, you should -
options: Flash your lights to let other vehicles know that you are coming.
Drive carefully and approach at a speed which gives you good time to avoid traffic which might suddenly appear.
Come to a complete stop before you come to the intersection. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 21 of 121

text: Where should you look when following a car?
options: Over or through the car you are following as well as watching its brake lights.
At the car's brake lights.
To the right-hand side of the car you are following.

text: When two lanes merge into one (as shown in the diagram), who should give way?
options: The vehicle which has to cross the lane line.
The faster vehicle.
The vehicle in the right-hand lane because it is overtaking.
explanation: The vehicle which has to cross the lane line. That reduces risk since lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: When you see an oncoming vehicle you should -
options: Swerve to avoid it, while braking.
Create a buffer between you and the other vehicle.
Always slow down.

text: When you see this sign you must -
options: Slow down and be prepared to stop only if there is any danger of a collision with another vehicle or pedestrian.
Stop at the stop line and give way to all traffic.
Stop at the stop line and give way to all traffic on your right only. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 82 of 121

text: When driving in an area where there are many pedestrians (e.g. a bus stop) it is important to -
options: Slow down and watch for an indication that they will enter the road.
Increase your speed to avoid the chance of hitting them.
Put your headlights on high beam so they can see you better.

text: When it is very foggy during the day or night and your vehicle has no fog lights, you should -
options: Follow closer to other vehicles.
Put on your high beam lights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights to make your vehicle seen.

text: When taking a left curve you should -
options: Plan to finish in the left part of your lane.
Lean your motorcycle and apply the brakes throughout the corner.
Brake as late as possible to maintain your speed and balance.

text: When the road is marked this way are you permitted to cross the lines to overtake the bicycle rider if the way forward is clear?
options: Yes.
Yes, only if it is one-way traffic.
No.

text: When you see this sign, what must you do?
options: Drive quickly over the railway crossing.
Stop before the railway crossing, wait for 1 minute and proceed if the crossing is clear.
Slow down and be ready to stop and give way to a train. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 85 of 121

text: You should expect this sign, if -
options: A give way sign at an intersection is ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop.
You are approaching a school or playground.
You are approaching an intersection with traffic lights, be prepared to stop.
explanation: A give way sign at an intersection is ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop. It helps because giving way prevents conflicts with traffic that has priority.

text: Which of the following statements relating to motorcyclists and bicycle riders is correct?
options: Alcohol affects their sense of balance.
Alcohol improves their concentration.
Alcohol improves their reflexes and judgement.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Sharp bend to the right ahead, slow down and drive carefully.
Turn around and go back, you are going the wrong way.
No right turn allowed.
explanation: Sharp bend to the right ahead, slow down and drive carefully. It helps because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: You are approaching the start of a T2 transit lane. You are the only person in the car. You want to turn left at the next intersection 200 metres away. Can you travel in the transit lane at this point?
options: No, because you can only travel in the transit lane if the intersection you are turning left at is within 100 metres.
Yes, because you only have a short distance to drive.
Yes, if there is no traffic behind you.
explanation: No, because you can only travel in the transit lane if the intersection you are turning left at is within 100 metres. It helps because special lanes keep high-occupancy or public transport moving, and misuse disrupts flow.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Slow down, be ready to stop and give way to all vehicles already on the roundabout if there is a danger of a collision.
All traffic must turn back at the roundabout.
Stop at all times and give way to all traffic on your right.
explanation: Slow down, be ready to stop and give way to all vehicles already on the roundabout if there is a danger of a collision. It is safer because giving way prevents conflicts with traffic that has priority.

text: If you take medicine and then drink alcohol -
options: The alcohol will have less effect than if taken alone.
Your ability to react to emergencies will improve.
It can have a bad effect on your driving ability. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 8 of 121 AD005 - Having 1 or 2 alcoholic drinks before driving -
Has no effect on your driving ability.
Improves your driving ability.
Will affect your reactions and judgement.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Traffic controller ahead, be prepared to stop.
You are approaching the end of a road work zone.
Road closed ahead.

text: A friend lends you a van that has seats for ten passengers. What type of licence do you need to drive this type of vehicle?
options: A small bus licence.
A car licence.
A heavy rigid vehicle licence.

text: When riding on a wet or slippery road riders should -
options: Ride at a normal constant speed as sign posted for the area.
Reduce speed so that it requires less time if they need to stop.
Ride around with their hands on the brake lever and foot on the brake pedal in case they have to stop in a hurry.

text: On a wet road how do you make an emergency stop?
options: Apply the rear brake only.
Apply the front and rear brakes together.
Apply the front brake only if the rear wheel begins to slide.

text: When you see this sign you should -
options: Not drive beyond the sign.
Drive with caution.
Not pass another vehicle.
explanation: Not drive beyond the sign. That reduces risk since signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: The adult passenger in the rear is breaking the law because she is -
options: Not wearing the available seat belt.
Sitting in the back seat.
Distracting the driver.

options: Every few seconds so that you always know what is behind you.
Before you accelerate or brake so that you do not force people to change their speed.
Before every ride.
explanation: Every few seconds so that you always know what is behind you. Frequent mirror checks keep you aware of traffic behind so you can ride predictably.

text: Safety tips when driving near a cyclist, choose the correct answer –
options: Bicycle riders are more difficult to see than cars or trucks, especially at night.
Always check for bicycle riders whenever you travel on the road, particularly when turning at intersection.
All of the above.

text: Which sign painted on the road tells you there is a pedestrian crossing ahead?
options: B
A
C
explanation: B. It helps because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: If you hold a learner or provisional licence class what is the Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) limit?
options: Zero.

text: Double unbroken dividing lines are marked on a roadway. You may -
options: Cross them to make a U turn.
Cross them to overtake a car ahead if it is safe to do so.
Cross them to turn into a driveway or property, or overtake a cyclist if it is safe to do so. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 30 of 121

text: Are cyclists allowed to ride side by side on the road, up to two abreast?
options: No, they cyclists should only ride in single file.
Yes, overtake the cyclists as you would a car, when safe to do so.
No, drivers should use their horn to make the cyclists move to one side.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Watch out for bicycle riders along the roadway or when turning.
Bicycle riders not allowed on the roadway.
You are approaching a children's playground, slow down.
explanation: Watch out for bicycle riders along the roadway or when turning. It is safer because cyclists are vulnerable, and consistent rules keep their movements predictable.

text: Police officers may check that you are correctly licensed when -
options: You are riding as a pillion passenger with a licensed rider.
You are purchasing a motorcycle from a motorcycle dealer.
You are involved in an accident, stopped after committing a traffic offence, or stopped for Random Breath Testing whilst riding your motorcycle.

text: When riding on a bumpy road -
options: Rise slightly on the footrests so that you can absorb the shock with your knees and elbows.
Keep your normal seating position.
Take your feet off the footpegs.

text: When passengers get in the car and do not put their seat belts on, the safest thing to do is -
options: Tell them the car has seat belts and they should wear them.
Say nothing because it's the passengers' responsibility to wear their seat belts.
Drive slower than you normally would so the passengers are safe.
explanation: Tell them the car has seat belts and they should wear them. This matters because restraints keep occupants in place and reduce injury in a crash.

text: You are in car A and are going straight ahead through the intersection. Who should give way?
options: Car B.
Whoever gets to the intersection first.
Car A.
explanation: Car B. It helps because right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: What is meant by this sign on or near a bridge?
options: Stop at all times before crossing the bridge and only give way to pedestrians who may be crossing.
Do not overtake a vehicle travelling in the same direction.
Slow down and be prepared to give way to vehicles travelling in the opposite direction.

text: You wish to turn left at this intersection. The traffic lights are red and you see this sign. You should -
options: Stop, then if you see it is safe turn left.
Stop until the light turns green.
Stop then go straight ahead.
explanation: Stop, then if you see it is safe turn left. It is safer because stopping prevents you entering a conflict or hazard unexpectedly.

text: In wet weather when it becomes hard for you to see, you should -
options: Turn on your headlights, slow down, and double your following distance behind the vehicle in front.
Flash your headlights to warn other drivers.
Turn your headlights on high beam.

text: You are facing traffic lights (as shown). What do they mean?
options: You may proceed only in the direction of the green arrow.
You may proceed only in the direction of the green arrow when the red light has changed to green.
You must give way to oncoming traffic.
explanation: You may proceed only in the direction of the green arrow. That reduces risk since lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: If both vehicles P and O in the diagram are turning right, which vehicle is in the best position to turn left into the street marked 'X'?
options: Vehicle O.
Vehicle P.
Neither vehicle.
explanation: Vehicle O. That reduces risk since right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: You approach an intersection in busy traffic and want to go straight ahead. The traffic lights turn green. When are you permitted to enter the intersection?
options: When the vehicle behind signals you to go.
Only when there is room for your vehicle on the other side.
Immediately after the traffic lights turn green.

text: You want to park your vehicle for a short time. It is night time. You should -
options: Pick a visible position or leave the parking or hazard lights on.
Park on the footpath.
Leave your headlights on high beam.
explanation: Pick a visible position or leave the parking or hazard lights on. It helps because reduced visibility means hazards appear later and take longer to react to.

text: If you are driving and it starts to rain, you should -
options: Put your lights on high beam so you can see better.
Put your hazard warning lights on and increase your speed to avoid the rain.
Slow down using the brake gently, since rain and oil on the road may create a slippery surface.

text: To turn back into the same road from which you joined this roundabout you must -
options: Stay in the right lane all the way round.
Move into the left lane to leave the roundabout.
Use the left lane all the way round.
explanation: Stay in the right lane all the way round. It helps because roundabouts rely on lane discipline and giving way to avoid side impacts.

text: When you see older people on or near the road, you should -
options: Slow down and take extra care because they may not see you until you are very close.
Sound your horn and keep going at the same speed so you do not hold up the traffic.
Drive around them to keep the traffic moving.

text: When making a right-hand turn at the intersection shown, you must give way to -
options: A vehicle approaching from your left and intending to turn right.
An oncoming vehicle going straight ahead or turning left, and any vehicle on your right.
Only pedestrians. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 13 of 121

text: When being overtaken by another vehicle what should you do to help?
options: Move to the left and stop.
Brake quickly to let the other vehicle overtake.
Keep left and allow plenty of room to let the other vehicle back in. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 43 of 121

text: In addition to wearing a motorcycle helmet you should -
options: Ensure that you always wear motorcycle specific clothing.
Make sure that you also wear sunglasses for additional protection.
Wear a hair-net to help your helmet last longer.
explanation: Ensure that you always wear motorcycle specific clothing. Motorcycle gear is built for abrasion and impact, unlike casual clothing.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: T-intersection ahead. If you are on the terminating road, you must give way to all vehicles approaching from your right or left.
No through road ahead, slow down.
Tollway ahead, be prepared to stop and pay toll.
explanation: T-intersection ahead. If you are on the terminating road, you must give way to all vehicles approaching from your right or left. That reduces risk since giving way prevents conflicts with traffic that has priority.

text: You are in busy traffic and slow down for a bicycle rider. A driver behind you beeps a horn and pressures you to go around the bike and drive faster. How should you respond?
options: Go slower because the slower you go the safer you are.
Resist the pressure, stay calm and overtake the cyclist when it is safe.
Overtake the bike quickly and speed up to stop the other driver becoming aggressive.

text: You wish to turn left here. The pedestrian lights are flashing red. You should -
options: Move into the right hand lane.
Slowly move through the intersection turning left.
Give way to pedestrians still crossing.

text: When driving in an area where there are many pedestrians (e.g. a bus stop) it is important to -
options: Slow down and watch for an indication that they will enter the road.
Put your headlights on high beam so they can see you better.
Increase your speed to avoid the chance of hitting them.
explanation: Slow down and watch for an indication that they will enter the road. It helps because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: You hear the siren of an ambulance approaching you from behind. You should -
options: Continue at the same speed.
Slow down to the speed of other traffic.
Move into the left lane.

text: When riding and wearing brightly coloured clothing you will -
options: Dazzle other motorists on the road.
Create a hazard by distracting other drivers.
Be seen more easily by other motorists.

text: If you wear regular spectacles while you ride -
options: You should also wear a face shield or visor.
You need no other eye protection.
You must not ride at night.

text: At a pedestrian crossing with traffic lights, when the amber light starts 'flashing' after the red stop signal, it means -
options: You may carefully drive through the crossing, if there is no risk of colliding with pedestrians.
The traffic lights are out of order and pedestrians must not use the crossing.
The green light is due. Do not proceed until the green light appears.
explanation: You may carefully drive through the crossing, if there is no risk of colliding with pedestrians. It is safer because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: Seat belts and child restraints (eg baby capsules and child seats) -
options: Must always be worn properly, and adjusted tightly.
Are only needed on long trips.
Are only needed on short trips.
explanation: Must always be worn properly, and adjusted tightly. It helps because restraints keep occupants in place and reduce injury in a crash.

text: In this roundabout with two lanes, can the marked car turn right?
options: No, not at any time.
Yes, at any time.
Yes, after changing to the right hand lane.
explanation: No, not at any time. It is safer because roundabouts rely on lane discipline and giving way to avoid side impacts.

text: If you are stopped by Police while riding a motorcycle on a road or road related area and you are not carrying your rider's licence you could expect to be -
options: Told to go home and get it.
Given an on-the-spot fine or summonsed to Court by Police.
Given twelve hours to produce it at your local Police Station.

text: A GIVE WAY sign at an intersection means that you must -
options: Be ready to stop and give way to all other traffic if there is danger of a collision.
Stop completely at all times and have no right of way.
Slow down and only give way to traffic on your right.
explanation: Be ready to stop and give way to all other traffic if there is danger of a collision. It helps because giving way prevents conflicts with traffic that has priority.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: There is a lane just for light rail vehicles.
You are approaching a lane that is only for buses.
Slow down and prepare to stop for a train.
explanation: There is a lane just for light rail vehicles. It is safer because lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: This bridge has only just enough room for two vehicles. As you come close to it you should -
options: Slow down and pay extra attention.
Sound your horn to warn the other driver.
Maintain your speed, keeping to the limit.
explanation: Slow down and pay extra attention. This matters because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: You approach a person crossing the road. You should -
options: Slow down or stop to avoid hitting the person.
Slow down and sound your horn to hurry up the person.
Maintain your speed and swerve around the person.
explanation: Slow down or stop to avoid hitting the person. That reduces risk since pedestrians are vulnerable and need extra protection.

text: When you see this sign you should -
options: Drive carefully, you are reaching the top of the hill and will not be able to see a safe distance in front of you.
Watch out, the road ahead may be flooded.
Slow down, there is a dangerous curve ahead. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 86 of 121

text: As you leave a freeway, which of the following should you check?
options: Your speed.
Fuel gauge.
Windscreen wipers.
explanation: Your speed. It is safer because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: To make yourself more visible to oncoming vehicles during the day -
options: Ride with your headlight on low beam.
Ride with your headlight off.
Flash your brake light every now and then.
explanation: Ride with your headlight on low beam. Low beam during the day makes you more visible without dazzling other road users.

text: If an oncoming vehicle crosses the centre line and is coming straight at you and you cannot stop, you should -
options: Brake, look for room to the left, sound your horn and flash your lights.
Slow down and hope that the driver will turn away.
Drive onto the wrong side of the road and hope the other vehicle does not do the same.
explanation: Brake, look for room to the left, sound your horn and flash your lights. That reduces risk since predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: If you are driving a bus, taxi, hire-car, heavy motor vehicle (over 13.9 tonnes Gross Vehicle Mass), or a vehicle with a dangerous load, it is an offence when the level of alcohol in your blood reaches -
explanation: 0.02. It helps because alcohol and drugs slow reactions and impair judgment.

text: Is it best to change gears before, during or after a turn?
options: Before.
After.
During.
explanation: Before. Changing gears mid-corner can unsettle the bike; set the gear before you lean.

text: This person is standing on a pedestrian refuge. If he steps out onto your lane you should -
options: Give way to the person if there is any danger of colliding.
Slow down and sound the horn to warn the person to move back.
Maintain your speed so you do not hold up the traffic.
explanation: Give way to the person if there is any danger of colliding. It is safer because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: Can a P Plate (provisional) driver legally instruct a learner driver?
options: Yes, provided the provisional driver has held a P Plate license for more than 6 months.
No.
Yes, provided plates are displayed.

text: What could be the penalties for driving over the speed limit -
options: Fines, demerit points and possibly loss of licence.
Fines only.
A letter of warning and a small fine.

text: You are being overtaken by a car on a two-laned road. In what part of the lane should you ride?
options: The centre or left of your lane.
No special part of your lane.
The far right of your lane.

text: This light means, you -
options: Can go straight ahead, or turn left or turn right, if it is safe to do so.
Must stop and wait for the red light before proceeding.
Can make a U turn provided it is safe to do so.
explanation: Can go straight ahead, or turn left or turn right, if it is safe to do so. It helps because lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: If a vehicle you are driving is involved in an accident and a person is injured, what must you do after stopping?
options: Render every assistance and take immediate steps to have an ambulance notified. Then call the Police.
Only call the Police if the accident also resulted in over $500 worth of property damage.
Report the accident to Police within seven days.
explanation: Render every assistance and take immediate steps to have an ambulance notified. Then call the Police. That reduces risk since getting help quickly reduces harm and keeps the scene safe.

text: You wish to turn left at this intersection. The traffic lights are red and you see this sign. You should -
options: Stop, then if you see it is safe turn left.
Stop then go straight ahead.
Stop until the light turns green.

text: Why should you avoid heavy braking on a wet road?
options: Your wheels may skid and cause a loss of control.
If the wheels lock up your handbrake may not work.
You might wet pedestrians walking along the footpath.
explanation: Your wheels may skid and cause a loss of control. That reduces risk since wet roads reduce grip and increase stopping distance.

text: When riding a motorcycle at night you should -
options: Reduce speed even on roads you know well as you cannot see very far ahead at night.
Ride at all times with your headlight on high beam to give you better vision.
Ride as you normally would in daytime.
explanation: Reduce speed even on roads you know well as you cannot see very far ahead at night. At night you can see less road ahead, so you need extra stopping distance.

text: What could be the penalties for driving over the speed limit -
options: Fines, demerit points and possibly loss of licence.
Fines only.
A letter of warning and a small fine.
explanation: Fines, demerit points and possibly loss of licence. It is safer because severe penalties deter dangerous or unethical behavior.

text: You are in the right hand lane and are planning to go straight ahead through this roundabout. When should you signal left to exit the roundabout?
options: After point O.
After point N.
After point M.
explanation: After point O. That reduces risk since roundabouts rely on lane discipline and giving way to avoid side impacts.

text: You need to stop quickly, you should use -
options: Both brakes together.
The front brake only.
The rear brake only.

text: Are you allowed to use a hand-held mobile phone while driving a car?
options: Yes, but you must hold the steering wheel with at least one hand.
No.
Yes, but only when you stop at intersections. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 102 of 121

text: If there are no signs or markings to advise you, can you choose any of these methods of parking?
options: No, only N is correct.
Yes. M, N and O are all legal.
Yes, N is best but M and O are quite legal.
explanation: No, only N is correct. It helps because parking safely and being visible prevents collisions and obstruction.

text: You are going to turn right from a one-way street. Where should you be when you start your turn?
options: Position R. As close as possible to the right side of the road.
Any position if it is safe to do so.
Position M. From the middle of the road.
explanation: Position R. As close as possible to the right side of the road. That reduces risk since lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: What should you be able to see in each mirror fitted to your motorcycle?
options: About half of the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you.
The lane behind.
Your shoulder and the lane behind.

text: The faster the vehicle in front of you is travelling, the -
options: More distance and time you need to overtake.
Less time you need to overtake.
Closer you must get before starting to overtake.
explanation: More distance and time you need to overtake. It is safer because careless actions create unpredictable conflicts.

text: This sign means you should -
options: Drive carefully, roundabout ahead.
Pass to the left of the sign.
Turn left at next street. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 65 of 121

text: Other protective options to wear when riding include -
options: Back protectors to protect your spine and kidney belts.
Nylon jacket and pants.
Light cotton shirt and pants.

text: You want to leave your automatic car parked on a street sloping uphill. You should -
options: Put the handbrake on and put the transmission in "P" (park).
Park only on flat areas.
Turn the wheels away from the kerb.
explanation: Put the handbrake on and put the transmission in "P" (park). It helps because parking safely and being visible prevents collisions and obstruction.

text: What is this driver doing that is negligent and illegal?
options: Crossing an unbroken line at a curve.
Not signaling to change lanes.
Overtaking on the kerb side.

text: You buy a car and find that the spare tyre is smooth; the tread is only just visible. If you get a puncture will it be legal to drive the car with a smooth spare tyre?
options: No, it's illegal to drive a car with a smooth tyre even if it is the spare.
Yes, but you must get the puncture fixed within 24 hours.
Yes, if the tyre is correctly inflated and the side walls of the tyre are in good condition.
explanation: No, it's illegal to drive a car with a smooth tyre even if it is the spare. This matters because worn tyres lose grip and are illegal, increasing stopping distance and blowout risk.

text: When you see this sign you should –
options: Not pass another vehicle.
Not drive beyond the sign.
Drive with caution.

text: To stop a motorcycle well, you should always use -
options: Both brakes together.
Only the front brake at high speed.
Only the rear brake at high speed.
explanation: Both brakes together. Using both brakes balances the bike and shortens stopping distance.

text: When driving past parked vehicles, which of the following is it most important to do -
options: Watch for pedestrians, animals and car doors opening.
Drive in the right-hand lane, if there is one.
Stay as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 51 of 121

text: You are riding a motorcycle and following a large vehicle at 80km/h. You should position yourself -
options: To the left of the road to make it easier to be seen.
Close behind the vehicle to keep out of the wind.
Well back so that you can see past the vehicle.

text: If your throttle sticks while in traffic, what is the first thing you should do?
options: Sound your horn to warn other vehicles.
Rotate the throttle back and forth several times.
Immediately squeeze the clutch lever, turn off the engine at the cut-off switch and apply the brakes.

text: As you approach a set of traffic lights at an intersection, they change from green to yellow (amber). You must:
options: Stop before the lights, unless you are so close that sudden braking might cause an accident.
Accelerate to clear the intersection before the lights change to red.
Drive through the intersection without accelerating.

text: At the T-intersection shown in the diagram which vehicle should give way?
options: Vehicle R.
Vehicle Q.
Whichever vehicle got there last.
explanation: Vehicle R. It is safer because right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: When you wish to drive straight ahead at a roundabout you may enter from either the left or right lane. As you continue around you should -
options: Move into another lane with least traffic.
Change lanes to get through quickly.
Keep in the lane you entered the roundabout. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 26 of 121

text: When you wish to turn left at a roundabout you indicate -
options: Left from start to finish.
Only if you think it necessary.
Left only after you enter the roundabout.

text: Sticking your knees out when cornering your motorcycle on a road -
options: Is not a good or efficient style of riding on a road.
Is a tried and proven method of cornering.
Will make you corner faster.
explanation: Is not a good or efficient style of riding on a road. On the road it reduces stability and clearance without adding useful control.

text: When approaching a railway level crossing displaying this sign, you must –
options: Continue across at normal speed, do not slow down.
Slow down, look both ways for trains and be prepared to stop if necessary.
Increase your speed to avoid any approaching trains. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 20 of 121

text: You have a six year old child with you in your car. You have just parked so you can collect a prescription from the chemist. You should -
options: Leave the child in the car.
Take the child with you.
Ask an older person sitting nearby to watch the child.

text: Bicycle and motorcycle riders have the same rights to use the road as other motor vehicle drivers. They are, however, more at risk in traffic because -
options: They are harder to see in traffic and do not have the same protection as many drivers.
They are careless and do not obey road rules.
They ride too fast and do not turn their lights on.
explanation: They are harder to see in traffic and do not have the same protection as many drivers. That reduces risk since cyclists are vulnerable, and consistent rules keep their movements predictable.

text: You are most likely to find this sign -
options: If an unsealed road is ahead.
As you approach a winding road, slow down and drive with caution.
If there is a steep hill ahead.

text: It is 9.20am on a school day. You are driving at 60 km/h, the same speed as traffic around you. You pass this sign but the other cars do not slow down much. What should you do?
options: Slow down immediately to 40 km/h or less even though other drivers want to go faster.
Drive at the speed of the other drivers because it is safer to go with the flow of traffic than slow others up.
Stay at 60 km/h because it is nearly 9.30am and the times on the school sign are only advisory.
explanation: Slow down immediately to 40 km/h or less even though other drivers want to go faster. That reduces risk since children can be unpredictable and may step out without warning.

text: You are driving at night with your headlights on high beam. When should you dip your headlights?
options: Never, you are allowed to drive with your lights on high beam at all times.
When within 200 metres of an oncoming vehicle only.
When within 200 metres of the vehicle ahead or an oncoming one. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 2 of 121

text: When riding past parked cars motorcycle riders should -
options: Create sufficient space from the cars to avoid opening doors or people stepping from between the cars.
Flash the bike's headlight as a warning to anyone in or near the cars.
Be ready to sound their horn if someone should open a door or step from between the cars.
explanation: Create sufficient space from the cars to avoid opening doors or people stepping from between the cars. Extra space protects you from opening doors and people stepping out.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Drive carefully, and watch out for kangaroos entering the road for the next 30 km.
Zoo 30 km ahead.
Nature reserve 30 km ahead.
explanation: Drive carefully, and watch out for kangaroos entering the road for the next 30 km. This matters because animals are unpredictable and can enter the road suddenly.

text: What does this sign mean?
