options: One way traffic ahead.
Stop sign ahead, slow down and prepare to stop.
You are approaching a roundabout, prepare to give way.

text: Right-turns must be made from which lanes when travelling on a laned roadway?
options: The far right-hand lane or any other lane having an arrow pointing right.
The lane carrying the least amount of traffic.
The far left-hand lane.
explanation: The far right-hand lane or any other lane having an arrow pointing right. It is safer because right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: You are in busy traffic and slow down for a bicycle rider. A driver behind you beeps a horn and pressures you to go around the bike and drive faster. How should you respond?
options: Resist the pressure, stay calm and overtake the cyclist when it is safe.
Overtake the bike quickly and speed up to stop the other driver becoming aggressive.
Go slower because the slower you go the safer you are.
explanation: Resist the pressure, stay calm and overtake the cyclist when it is safe. That reduces risk since cyclists are vulnerable, and consistent rules keep their movements predictable.

text: When approaching a turn on your motorcycle you should -
options: Leave your braking until you are in the turn so you do not lose too much speed.
Cover your brakes in case you need them while in the turn.
Slow down before the turn and increase your speed gradually as you come out of the turn.

text: There are no traffic signs or signals at an intersection. If you intend to drive through the intersection, you must give way to -
options: An oncoming vehicle about to turn right.
Vehicles on your left only.
Vehicles on your right.

text: The traffic on the other side of this intersection has stopped. You are in the car shown and want to cross the intersection. The lights are green. What should you do?
options: Wait until there is enough room for your vehicle to cross the intersection completely.
Drive through the intersection slowly and hope that it will clear before the lights change.
Drive into the intersection and then turn left.
explanation: Wait until there is enough room for your vehicle to cross the intersection completely. This matters because right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: If you see a horse and rider on the road what should you do?
options: Slow down and give them plenty of room.
Sound your horn to warn the rider.
Speed up to pass the horse.
explanation: Slow down and give them plenty of room. That reduces risk since animals are unpredictable and can enter the road suddenly.

text: When you come across roadworks -
options: You must obey the signs that are displayed at all times.
You only have to obey the signs when there are workers about.
You only have to obey the signs during working hours.
explanation: You must obey the signs that are displayed at all times. This matters because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: Speed limit signs (such as the one shown) tell drivers -
options: The maximum speed they are allowed to drive.
The minimum speed they are allowed to drive.
The recommended speed they are allowed to drive.
explanation: The maximum speed they are allowed to drive. It is safer because higher speeds increase stopping distance and crash severity.

text: If turning right at a T-intersection (as shown) must you give way to vehicles approaching from both the left and right?
options: Yes, whether they are turning or not.
No, only the vehicle on the right.
No, you have right of way.
explanation: Yes, whether they are turning or not. It is safer because right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: What may you do at an intersection with traffic lights at which this sign is displayed?
options: You may turn left only if a green arrow is shown.
You should slow down and check if anyone is coming before turning left.
If the lights are red you must first stop, then you may turn left if it is safe to do so.

text: When driving past parked vehicles, which of the following is it most important to do -
options: Watch for pedestrians, animals and car doors opening.
Drive in the right-hand lane, if there is one.
Stay as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
explanation: Watch for pedestrians, animals and car doors opening. That reduces risk since pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Do not drive with your lights on high beam.
A sharp depression in the road is ahead, be prepared, slow down.
Police station ahead. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 72 of 121

text: Properly adjusted mirrors will allow you to see -
options: Into the lane beside you.
Only behind you.
About half of the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane beside you.

text: You want to turn left at this roundabout. Which lane must you use?
options: Lane A.
Lane B.
Either lane.

text: If you are not sure you have enough distance to overtake a vehicle ahead, you should -
options: Sound your horn to signal the driver ahead to slow down.
Put the vehicle in a lower gear and speed up.
Wait for a better opportunity with more distance to overtake.

text: Which statement is true?
options: You must give way to pedestrians if there is any danger of hitting them.
Pedestrians have no special rights on the roads.
You must give way to pedestrians only at marked crossings.
explanation: You must give way to pedestrians if there is any danger of hitting them. That reduces risk since pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Do not litter.
Children's playground ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop.
Workers ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Vehicles carrying three or more people, and motorcycles may use this lane.
Motor cars carrying one passenger may use this lane.
This lane is reserved for bicycle riders only.
explanation: Vehicles carrying three or more people, and motorcycles may use this lane. That reduces risk since signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Railway level crossing ahead, slow down and look out for trains, be prepared to stop.
Cattle or sheep crossing the road ahead, drive slowly.
Give way sign ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop.
explanation: Railway level crossing ahead, slow down and look out for trains, be prepared to stop. It is safer because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: When you are driving on a two-lane freeway, which lane should you choose?
options: The left lane unless you are overtaking.
Whichever lane has the least traffic.
The right lane to avoid slow-moving vehicles.
explanation: The left lane unless you are overtaking. This matters because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: What should a pillion passenger do when you stop?
options: Place the same foot on the ground as the rider.
Place both feet on the ground.
Keep both feet on the foot pegs.

text: You come to an intersection in Sydney with a Light Rail vehicle about to enter. What should you do?
options: Wait until the intersection is clear.
Enter the intersection, but keep away from the Light Rail vehicle.
Change lanes before crossing the intersection.
explanation: Wait until the intersection is clear. This matters because trains cannot stop quickly, so you only proceed when the crossing is clear.

text: If you are driving through a road work zone in the left hand lane and you see this sign you should -
options: Stop and wait for directions.
Speed up to get in front of any cars traveling in the right hand lane.
Merge to the right and give way to other traffic.

text: Before driving a long distance at fast speed or carrying a full car load, you should -
options: Check your tyre pressure, and if necessary, increase it to what the manufacturer recommends.
Make sure you have a street directory, so you know where you are going.
Have a large meal and a cup of coffee.
explanation: Check your tyre pressure, and if necessary, increase it to what the manufacturer recommends. That reduces risk since higher speeds increase stopping distance and crash severity.

text: When driving on a multi-lane road with a speed limit of more than 80 km/h, which lane should you choose?
options: Either left or right lane.
The left lane unless overtaking.
The right lane to avoid slow moving vehicles.

text: At a pedestrian crossing with traffic lights, when the lights change to red you should -
options: Stop and continue after the pedestrians have crossed.
Slow down and give way to pedestrians.
Stop, wait for pedestrians to cross and for the green light to come on.

text: If you see a School Crossing Supervisor holding a sign like this, you must wait until the children -
options: Are off the crossing and the hand held sign is taken away.
Reach the right-hand side of the crossing.
Are out of sight.
explanation: Are off the crossing and the hand held sign is taken away. This matters because children can be unpredictable and may step out without warning.

text: You wish to go straight ahead on this roundabout with two lanes. Which lane may you use?
options: Either lane.
Left lane only.
Right lane only.
explanation: Either lane. That reduces risk since roundabouts rely on lane discipline and giving way to avoid side impacts.

text: Good control of your motorcycle may be achieved by -
options: Adopting a correct relaxed riding position.
Gripping the handlebars as tightly as possible.
Sitting as far back on the seat as possible to give the rear tyre more grip.

text: If there are no lanes marked on the road, you should drive -
options: Near to the left-hand side of the road.
Anywhere on your side of the road.
Along the middle of the road.
explanation: Near to the left-hand side of the road. This matters because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: In this diagram which light is most likely to make the motorcycle more noticeable to the car driver?
options: The right turn indicator.
The tail-light.
The headlight on high beam.

text: If you wear regular spectacles while you ride -
options: You must not ride at night.
You need no other eye protection.
You should also wear a face shield or visor.

text: You are going to make a turn. When should you apply the brakes?
options: While you are in the turn.
Before you start the turn.
As you come out of the turn.

text: What is the best way to avoid hitting other vehicles, people or animals when moving off from the kerb?
options: Sound your horn before moving away from the kerb to warn people of your intentions.
Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before moving off from the kerb.
Have a good look around while you walk up to your car and then drive off as soon as you can.

text: You are driving a car and want to pick up a passenger. The lane you want to stop in is a BUS LANE. Are you permitted to stop there?
options: No, unless you are driving a hire car or a taxi.
Yes, if you pick the passenger up and then immediately drive off.
Yes, you are allowed to stop in a BUS LANE for as long as you like.
explanation: No, unless you are driving a hire car or a taxi. That reduces risk since special lanes keep high-occupancy or public transport moving, and misuse disrupts flow.

text: If you are not sure you have enough distance to overtake a vehicle ahead, you should -
options: Wait for a better opportunity with more distance to overtake.
Put the vehicle in a lower gear and speed up.
Sound your horn to signal the driver ahead to slow down.
explanation: Wait for a better opportunity with more distance to overtake. This matters because overtake only when the road is clear and it is safe for all traffic.

text: Where must L or P plates be displayed on a vehicle -
options: Anywhere including on the dashboard.
Anywhere inside the windows but only if they are not tinted.
On the front and back of the exterior of the vehicle.

text: Even if the signal at a railway level crossing does not indicate that a train is coming, you should -
options: Speed up and cross the tracks quickly.
Stop completely at all times.
Slow down, be ready to stop and give way if there is danger of collision.

text: If you are driving along the highway and come across road works with a reduced speed zone, you must -
options: Slow down to the new speed limit.
Drive through the road works zone as fast as you can to get past it.
Drive at the same speed as other vehicles.
explanation: Slow down to the new speed limit. That reduces risk since higher speeds increase stopping distance and crash severity.

text: When approaching a turn on your motorcycle you should -
options: Slow down before the turn and increase your speed gradually as you come out of the turn.
Leave your braking until you are in the turn so you do not lose too much speed.
Cover your brakes in case you need them while in the turn.
explanation: Slow down before the turn and increase your speed gradually as you come out of the turn. Brake and set speed before the turn so you are stable, then accelerate out with grip.

text: You are driving in a 60 km/h zone, with only one lane for traffic in your direction. You see a bus ahead (with this sign displayed on the rear) signalling its intention to pull out from a bus stop, you should -
options: Slow down, and give way to the bus as it has priority.
Sound your horn to stop the bus from pulling out.
Continue at your normal speed as the bus does not have priority.
explanation: Slow down, and give way to the bus as it has priority. It helps because letting buses merge keeps traffic flowing and avoids side-swipes.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: If traffic lights are out of order or the amber light is flashing, you must stop and give way to traffic as if you are at an intersection with stop signs.
Stop, red light camera in operation.
Stop at all times and give way to all traffic.
explanation: If traffic lights are out of order or the amber light is flashing, you must stop and give way to traffic as if you are at an intersection with stop signs. This matters because giving way prevents conflicts with traffic that has priority.

text: If you see a School Crossing Monitor holding a sign like this, you must wait until the children -
options: Reach the right-hand side of the crossing.
Are out of sight.
Are off the crossing and the hand held sign is taken away.

text: When you have started to overtake the car, you notice that its right indicator is flashing. You should -
options: Check your mirror and move back in behind the car.
Immediately brake to a stop.
Accelerate quickly to get past. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 47 of 121

text: When going on a long trip, out of the following which is the most important to do?
options: Get plenty of rest before starting out.
Make sure your horn is working.
Have a good meal before driving.
explanation: Get plenty of rest before starting out. This matters because staying alert and scanning early gives you time to react.

text: At low speeds, if the rear tyre goes flat what is the first thing you will notice?
options: Your brakes will not work.
The rear of the motorcycle will tend to slide from side to side.
The steering will feel heavy.

text: You are driving in busy traffic in a 60 km/h zone. You feel 60 km/h is a bit too fast for the conditions. What should you do?
options: Turn off the busy street and wait for traffic to clear.
Keep up with the other traffic because it's probably safe if the sign says 60 km/h.
Slow down to a speed that suits the conditions.

text: You drive up to an intersection with a stop sign. There is no painted stop line. Where should you stop?
options: Before coming to and as near to the intersection as possible.
At the point where you can see clearly in both directions.
At least five metres before the intersection.

text: You wish to make a right-hand turn from a ONE WAY STREET with no arrows marked on the roadway. You should position your vehicle -
options: On the right-hand side of the street.
In the middle of the street.
On the left-hand side of the street.
explanation: On the right-hand side of the street. That reduces risk since right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: In this diagram both vehicles O and P must pass through GIVE WAY signs before entering the intersection. Which vehicle goes first?
options: Vehicle P goes first.
It depends on who moves first.
Vehicle O goes first. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 15 of 121

text: You are approaching a green light in vehicle A. An ambulance sounding its siren is approaching the same intersection and has a red light. You should -
options: Slow down and stop if necessary to prevent getting in its way.
Keep driving because you have the green light.
Pull over to the left before you reach the intersection.
explanation: Slow down and stop if necessary to prevent getting in its way. It helps because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: You must give way to pedestrians -
options: At all times, if there is any danger of colliding with them, even if there is no marked crossing.
Only on marked foot crossings.
Only on marked foot crossings and traffic light pedestrian crossings. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 57 of 121

text: You are driving your vehicle along a street and want to stop for a short time. Are you allowed to double park your vehicle (that is stand it on the road alongside a parked car)?
options: No, never.
Yes, provided you do not leave the vehicle.
Yes, provided you stop for a short time only and turn on your hazard warning lights.
explanation: No, never. This matters because double parking blocks traffic and reduces visibility, increasing risk.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Follow the arrow unless you are turning right.
All traffic must travel in the direction of the arrow.
Road curves to the left ahead.

text: You wish to turn left at this intersection and the traffic lights are green. What should you do?
options: Move forward slowly, make the left turn and wait behind car A.
Enter the intersection and sound the horn.
Wait behind the stop line until there is room for you to enter the new road. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 39 of 121

text: You change lanes and then see you are in a lane where the T3 rule applies. There is no other traffic in this lane. You have one passenger. What should you do?
options: Change lanes as soon as it is safe because you are not permitted to travel in a T3 lane with only two people in your car.
Keep driving in the T3 lane because there is no other traffic in it.
Immediately pull over to the left and stop. Then wait until it is safe to continue in another lane.
explanation: Change lanes as soon as it is safe because you are not permitted to travel in a T3 lane with only two people in your car. It is safer because special lanes keep high-occupancy or public transport moving, and misuse disrupts flow.

text: You should expect this sign –
options: If a one lane bridge is ahead.
If a one way street is ahead.
When a divided road ends and two way traffic is ahead. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 76 of 121

text: To help prevent fatigue when riding you should -
options: Dress to protect yourself fully from wind, heat, cold and rain and not ride any longer than two hours at a time.
Stop and rest at least every four hours.
Ride in short sleeves shirt with no gloves to allow the wind to keep you awake.

text: What is the first thing to do if you have a blowout?
options: Hold the hand grips tightly. Gradually close the throttle and let the motorcycle slow down.
Brake lightly on the wheel with the good tyre.
Turn quickly off the road.

text: Many people crash within the first few years of driving. What is the best way of learning to drive on your own without crashing?
options: Start driving in daylight where it is not too busy and only drive in busier traffic as your driving gets better.
Drive as much as you can with friends on the way to parties.
Drive in every kind of traffic situation as soon as you get your licence.
explanation: Start driving in daylight where it is not too busy and only drive in busier traffic as your driving gets better. It helps because staying alert and scanning early gives you time to react.

text: When going on a long trip, out of the following which is the most important to do?
options: Get plenty of rest before starting out.
Have a good meal before driving.
Make sure your horn is working.

text: You wish to turn left at this roundabout. Which lane may you use?
options: Left lane.
Right lane.
Either lane.
explanation: Left lane. This matters because roundabouts rely on lane discipline and giving way to avoid side impacts.

text: When riding on a single lane road, a motorcycle rider -
options: Can legally use any part of the lane.
Must remain in the left of the lane at all times.
Must remain in the middle of the lane at all times.
explanation: Can legally use any part of the lane. Using the full lane lets you choose the safest position for visibility and space.

text: It is 3 o'clock in the morning. You cannot see any other traffic. You want to turn right. You may -
options: Turn right when you have waited one minute.
Turn right if it is safe to do so.
Not turn right while the arrow is red.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Steep down-grade in the road ahead, slow down.
Road ahead slippery when wet, drive carefully.
Road under repair, slow down.

text: You are approaching the crest (top of a hill) on a narrow road, the safest procedure is to -
options: Keep to the left and slow down.
Flash your headlights to warn oncoming traffic.
Increase your speed and sound your horn.
explanation: Keep to the left and slow down. It is safer because keeping left lets faster traffic pass and reduces conflict.

text: On a single laned road (as shown), you must always overtake another vehicle on its right except when -
options: The other vehicle is turning right.
You are travelling at more than 80 km/h.
The other vehicle is going slower than you.
explanation: The other vehicle is turning right. It helps because overtake only when the road is clear and it is safe for all traffic.

text: Sitting too far back on the seat of your motorcycle will -
options: Affect weight distribution making steering very light.
Give your rear tyre more grip for braking at speed.
Not affect the motorcycle noticeably.
explanation: Affect weight distribution making steering very light. Shifting weight off the front wheel makes steering light and less stable.

text: Are you allowed to use a hand-held mobile phone while driving a car?
options: No.
Yes, but only when you stop at intersections.
Yes, but you must hold the steering wheel with at least one hand.
explanation: No. It is safer because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: You are driving at night and there is no other traffic around you. When can you use your headlights on high beam?
options: On any road, even if there are street lights.
On any road where the speed limit is above 80 km/h.
Only on roads that do not have street lights.
explanation: On any road, even if there are street lights. This matters because reduced visibility means hazards appear later and take longer to react to.

text: This light means, you –
options: Can make a U-turn provided it is safe to do so.
Must stop and wait for the red light before proceeding.
Can go straight ahead, or turn left or turn right, if it is safe to do so. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 36 of 121

text: When you see this sign you –
options: May stop at any time to pick up or drop off passengers.
Must not stop here at any time.
Must not stop your vehicle at the kerb during the times shown. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 70 of 121

text: You should not drive across a railway level crossing when -
options: Traffic is blocking the other side.
You are towing a caravan.
A station is nearby.
explanation: Traffic is blocking the other side. That reduces risk since trains cannot stop quickly, so you only proceed when the crossing is clear.

text: Before taking any drugs and then driving it is most important to -
options: Know what the effects of the drug are.
Plan to have some other person with you.
Have some food in your stomach.
explanation: Know what the effects of the drug are. That reduces risk since alcohol and drugs slow reactions and impair judgment.

text: You are going to make a turn. When should you apply the brakes?
options: Before you start the turn.
As you come out of the turn.
While you are in the turn.

text: Sitting too far back on the seat of your motorcycle will -
options: Not affect the motorcycle noticeably.
Affect weight distribution making steering very light.
Give your rear tyre more grip for braking at speed.

text: If the police suspect you may have been involved in street or drag racing, they may take immediate action. Which one of the following is correct? The police may -
options: Take your vehicle from you and keep it stored for up to three months.
Take your vehicle to the local police station and keep it till the following morning.
Take your vehicle away and sell it at an auction.
explanation: Take your vehicle from you and keep it stored for up to three months. It helps because careless actions create unpredictable conflicts.

text: You drive up to an intersection with a stop sign. There is no painted stop line. Where should you stop?
options: Before coming to and as near to the intersection as possible.
At least five metres before the intersection.
At the point where you can see clearly in both directions.
explanation: Before coming to and as near to the intersection as possible. It is safer because right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: Which of the following statements relating to motorcyclists and bicycle riders is correct?
options: Alcohol improves their concentration.
Alcohol improves their reflexes and judgement.
Alcohol affects their sense of balance.

text: What may you do at an intersection with traffic lights at which this sign is displayed?
options: If the lights are red you must first stop, then you may turn left if it is safe to do so.
You should slow down and check if anyone is coming before turning left.
You may turn left only if a green arrow is shown.
explanation: If the lights are red you must first stop, then you may turn left if it is safe to do so. It is safer because lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: When driving through a road work you should -
options: Maintain current speed if the road is clear.
Slow down and look out for hazards.
Sound your horn.

text: This intersection does not have any traffic lights or signs. You are in car A and want to turn right. When can you go?
options: After the car going straight ahead has passed.
Before the car going straight ahead has passed.
As soon as you get to the intersection.
explanation: After the car going straight ahead has passed. It is safer because right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: Which vehicle in the diagram must give way?
options: Vehicle K.
Vehicle L.
Vehicle J.

text: After warming up the engine you leave the choke ON. What will this do?
options: Discharge the battery.
Use more fuel.
Use less fuel.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Vehicles are not allowed to stop at the kerb except in a medical emergency.
Vehicles must not stop at the kerb, except if picking up a passenger.
Vehicles must not stop at the kerb, unless picking up goods.
explanation: Vehicles are not allowed to stop at the kerb except in a medical emergency. It is safer because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: If your throttle sticks while in traffic, what is the first thing you should do?
options: Immediately squeeze the clutch lever, turn off the engine at the cut-off switch and apply the brakes.
Rotate the throttle back and forth several times.
Sound your horn to warn other vehicles.

text: You are driving an older relative for an appointment and are running late. They ask you to go faster to get there on time. You should -
options: Choose a safe speed and say you will not go any faster.
Take the advice of a more experienced driver and go faster where you can.
Drop them off at the train station. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 107 of 121

text: The motorcyclist wants to travel straight ahead through this roundabout. The rider should watch out for the marked car because the car -
options: May be leaving the roundabout.
Could be going too fast.
May stop suddenly.
explanation: May be leaving the roundabout. That reduces risk since roundabouts rely on lane discipline and giving way to avoid side impacts.

text: Before driving long distances, which of the following should you do?
options: Make sure your vehicle has enough fuel, oil, water and the correct tyre pressure.
Take your street directory in case you get lost.
Take something to calm your nerves before driving. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 91 of 121

text: Before driving a long distance or carrying a full car load, you should
options: Check your tyre pressure, and if necessary, increase it to what the manufacturer recommends.
Have a large meal and a cup of coffee.
Make sure you have a street directory, so you know where you are going.

text: When police officers are at intersections giving directions you must -
options: Wait for the traffic lights to start working again.
Always follow any instruction they give you.
Drive through the intersection as you normally would. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 23 of 121

text: You approach a crossing and see the scene in the picture. You should –
options: Slow down and drive through giving way to the children.
Slow down and stop until the supervisor takes down the sign.
Stop and wait for the children until your lane is clear.

text: If the vehicle you are driving is involved in an accident (regardless of the damage), what details must you give, to the other driver(s), if asked?
options: You must give your name and address, and provide the name and address of the vehicle's owner.
Only your name and address details if Police ask for them.
No details at all until you have contacted your insurance company.

text: A Shared Traffic Zone, where pedestrians and other road users can share the road safely has a speed limit of -
options: 10 Km/h.
20 Km/h.
50 Km/h.
explanation: 10 Km/h. It helps because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: A vehicle ahead of you has stopped at a pedestrian crossing. You -
options: Must not overtake the stopped vehicle.
May overtake the vehicle if there are no pedestrians on the crossing.
May overtake the vehicle provided no cars are coming the other way.
explanation: Must not overtake the stopped vehicle. This matters because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: Riders may make themselves more noticeable to car drivers by -
options: Riding closely behind cars.
Riding to the side of cars at all times.
Wearing bright, fluorescent or contrasting coloured clothing.

text: Recommended additional protection for riders includes -
options: Wearing kidney belts and back protectors.
Wearing water-proof clothing.
Wearing sunglasses under your visor.
explanation: Wearing kidney belts and back protectors. Back and kidney protection reduces injury in a fall or impact.

text: If you enter an intersection that is under the control of a traffic controller -
options: Stop at the intersection and then proceed slowly.
Sound your horn at the traffic controller and hope they get out of your way.
Follow the directions of the traffic controller.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Next main town 35 km to the right.
Slow down, the maximum safe speed around the next curve in the road is 35km/h.
Winding road ahead for next 35 km.

text: It is early morning and there is no other traffic about. You approach an intersection when the traffic lights change from green to yellow. What should you do?
options: Stop.
Keep going.
Drive through and sound your horn. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 115 of 121

text: Every time before you ride you should check -
options: That the headlight and stop light are working.
Your fuel tap is not on reserve.
The expiry date of your licence.

text: When there are no arrows marked on the road, left turns must be made from -
options: The far left-hand side of the road.
Either side of the road.
The middle of the road.

text: You want to turn left at this roundabout. Which lane must you use?
options: Lane A.
Lane B.
Either lane.
explanation: Lane A. It helps because roundabouts rely on lane discipline and giving way to avoid side impacts.

text: Which statement is correct?
options: Red light cameras take photographs of vehicles that enter intersections when the lights are red.
Red light cameras take photographs of vehicles that speed through intersections.
Red light cameras take photographs of vehicles that cross intersections when the lights are yellow.
explanation: Red light cameras take photographs of vehicles that enter intersections when the lights are red. That reduces risk since right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: When you slow down for a stop, you should -
options: Downshift before stopping.
Downshift only if there is traffic ahead of you.
Downshift after stopping.

text: Good control of your motorcycle may be achieved by -
options: Adopting a correct relaxed riding position.
Gripping the handlebars as tightly as possible.
Sitting as far back on the seat as possible to give the rear tyre more grip.
explanation: Adopting a correct relaxed riding position. A relaxed posture improves balance and lets you make smooth control inputs.

text: A GIVE WAY sign at an intersection means that you must -
options: Stop completely at all times and have no right of way.
Be ready to stop and give way to all other traffic if there is danger of a collision.
Slow down and only give way to traffic on your right. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 17 of 121

text: You are at an intersection and see a pedestrian crossing the road into which you are turning. You must -
options: Give way to the pedestrian.
Sound your horn to warn the pedestrian to get out of the way.
Swerve around the pedestrian to avoid hitting them.
explanation: Give way to the pedestrian. It is safer because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: You are approaching a road with a loose surface. What should you do?
options: Slow down.
Ride normally.
Speed up.

text: If you are driving along the highway and come across road works with a reduced speed zone, you must -
options: Drive through the road works zone as fast as you can to get past it.
Drive at the same speed as other vehicles.
Slow down to the new speed limit.

text: When there are no arrows marked on the road, left turns must be made from -
options: The far left-hand side of the road.
The middle of the road.
Either side of the road.
explanation: The far left-hand side of the road. It helps because right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: You are turning right from one of two right turn only lanes. How should you use your indicators?
options: Indicate with your right hand signal the same as any other right hand turn.
You should not indicate at all because it might confuse other drivers.
Indicating in this situation is optional. Give a right hand signal if you think it will help other road users.

text: If an oncoming vehicle crosses the centre line and is coming straight at you and you cannot stop, you should -
options: Slow down and hope that the driver will turn away.
Drive onto the wrong side of the road and hope the other vehicle does not do the same.
Brake, look for room to the left, sound your horn and flash your lights.

text: At night you should -
options: Leave a longer gap behind the vehicle in front.
Use your hazard warning lights when overtaking another vehicle.
Drive closer to the vehicle in front so they can see you better.
explanation: Leave a longer gap behind the vehicle in front. It helps because staying alert and scanning early gives you time to react.

text: Before driving on a freeway, which of the following should you do?
options: Make sure your vehicle has enough fuel, oil, water and the correct tyre pressure.
Take your street directory in case you get lost.
Take something to calm your nerves before driving.
explanation: Make sure your vehicle has enough fuel, oil, water and the correct tyre pressure. It helps because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: When entering or leaving a driveway you must -
options: Give way to bicycles, vehicles and pedestrians.
Stop and give way only to vehicles.
Blow your horn to warn other road users.
explanation: Give way to bicycles, vehicles and pedestrians. This matters because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: Consuming even small amounts of alcohol before riding may -
options: Affect your ability to control your motorcycle and make riding dangerous.
Help clear your mind by relaxing you.
Have no effect whatsoever on you.

text: You should not drive across a railway level crossing when -
options: You are towing a caravan.
A station is nearby.
Traffic is blocking the other side. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 92 of 121

text: What should be displayed upon an approved helmet?
options: An Australian Standards AS1698 sticker.
Bright stickers to make the helmet more visible to vehicle drivers.
A manufacturer's approval and checked by sticker.

text: It is early morning and there is no other traffic about. You approach an intersection when the traffic lights change from green to yellow. What should you do?
options: Stop.
Keep going.
Drive through and sound your horn.
explanation: Stop. That reduces risk since stopping prevents you entering a conflict or hazard unexpectedly.

text: A friend lends you his car. It is very noisy and blows a lot of smoke. He tells you the vehicle has been given a defect notice but it's still OK to drive it. What should you do?
options: Borrow the car but only drive on streets where the car will not be a danger to others.
Before you borrow the car check the defect notice to make sure it is legal to drive the car.
Borrow the car, but always drive it 10 km/h below the speed limit.

text: You approach a crossing and see the scene in the picture. You should -
options: Slow down and stop until the supervisor takes down the sign.
Slow down and drive through giving way to the children.
Stop and wait for the children until your lane is clear.
explanation: Slow down and stop until the supervisor takes down the sign. It helps because pedestrians are vulnerable and need extra protection.

text: You wish to turn left at this roundabout. Which lane may you use?
options: Right lane.
Left lane.
Either lane.

text: If your vehicle is involved in an accident (regardless of the damage), what details must you give, to the other driver(s), if asked?
options: You must let them see your licence, take details, and give the name and address of the vehicle's owner.
No details at all until you have contacted your insurance company.
Only your name and address details if a Policeman asks for them.
explanation: You must let them see your licence, take details, and give the name and address of the vehicle's owner. It helps because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: Do bicycle riders have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers and motorcycle riders?
options: Yes.
No, they must always ride on the footpath.
No, they must give way to cars at all times when riding on the road.
explanation: Yes. That reduces risk since cyclists are vulnerable, and consistent rules keep their movements predictable.

text: If you are a new driver and first start to drive at night you should -
options: Drive mainly on streets that you know well.
Drive mainly in unfamiliar streets.
Drive long distances to improve your concentration.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Drive carefully, and watch out for kangaroos entering the road for the next 30km.
Zoo 30 km ahead.
Nature reserve 30 km ahead. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 69 of 121

text: Your ability to concentrate can be affected by -
options: Fatigue, alcohol, drugs and the clothing you wear.
The type of motorcycle you ride.
Whether you are familiar with the road you are riding on.

text: You see these zig-zag marking in the road in front of you. What do they mean?
options: Look out for animals on the side of the road.
Take care and look out for pedestrians at a crossing.
Be careful because the road ahead is slippery. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 53 of 121

text: What does this sign mean?
options: There is a hump (sudden slope up and down) in the road ahead, slow down.
There is a tunnel ahead, turn on your headlights.
The road ahead is closed, go back.
explanation: There is a hump (sudden slope up and down) in the road ahead, slow down. It helps because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: A good riding position should feel comfortable and allow you to -
options: Ride faster in all traffic conditions.
Relax more and enjoy your riding.
Have fast effective use of the controls without affecting the balance.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: You must not turn to the left.
You must not turn to the left or the right.
You must not turn to the right.
explanation: You must not turn to the left. It is safer because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: Your overall stopping distance will be longer when riding -
options: With a passenger.
At night.
Up a hill.

text: When you see this sign you must -
options: Slow down and be prepared to stop and give way to all traffic if there is any danger of a collision.
Stop and give way to all traffic even if the intersection is clear.
Slow down and be prepared to give way to traffic on your right only, if there is any danger of a collision.
explanation: Slow down and be prepared to stop and give way to all traffic if there is any danger of a collision. This matters because giving way prevents conflicts with traffic that has priority.

text: If you have not ridden a particular motorcycle before, you should -
options: Allow extra stopping distance.
Use the rear brake only.
Not go faster than 30 km/h.

text: To reduce the effect of alcohol before driving or riding you should -
options: Wait. The time depends on how much you have drunk.
Drink black coffee.
Have a glass of water.
explanation: Wait. The time depends on how much you have drunk. That reduces risk since alcohol and drugs slow reactions and impair judgment.

text: When driving in traffic lanes (as shown in the diagram), you may change your lane -
options: Provided you sound your horn to warn other drivers.
Only when it is safe to do so.
Without looking, provided you use your indicator. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 31 of 121

text: In which of the situations shown are you permitted to do a U-turn?
options: Only turn shown in situation T is permitted.
Turns shown in situations Q and T are permitted.
Turns shown in situations T and Z are permitted.

text: If you take medicine and then drink alcohol -
options: It can have a particularly bad effect on your driving ability.
The alcohol will have less effect than if taken alone.
Your ability to react to emergencies will improve.
explanation: It can have a particularly bad effect on your driving ability. It is safer because alcohol and drugs slow reactions and impair judgment.

text: When driving near pedestrian crossings, intersections, or school crossings, you should always -
options: Slow down, watch for pedestrians and be ready to make a safe stop.
Move into the left lane.
Keep your eyes on the speedo.
explanation: Slow down, watch for pedestrians and be ready to make a safe stop. This matters because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: Right-turns must be made from which lanes when travelling on a laned roadway?
options: The far right-hand lane or any other lane having an arrow pointing right.
The lane carrying the least amount of traffic.
The far left-hand lane.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: All right lane traffic must turn right at the next intersection.
Right lane traffic may turn right or go straight ahead at the next intersection.
One way traffic ahead.
explanation: All right lane traffic must turn right at the next intersection. That reduces risk since signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: When is a motorcycle rider allowed to ride without an approved helmet?
options: Never.
When the rider has a medical certificate.
Only during daylight hours.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Only vehicles carrying a disable person and displaying a mobility parking authority may park in this area.
Motorcyclists may park in this area.
Vehicles may park in this area for up to ten minutes.
explanation: Only vehicles carrying a disable person and displaying a mobility parking authority may park in this area. That reduces risk since signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: When driving through temporary road work you should -
options: Slow down and look out for hazards.
Maintain current speed if the road is clear.
Sound your horn.
explanation: Slow down and look out for hazards. That reduces risk since careless actions create unpredictable conflicts.

text: Having 1 or 2 alcoholic drinks before driving -
options: Will affect your reactions and judgement.
Improves your driving ability.
Has no effect on your driving ability.
explanation: Will affect your reactions and judgement. It is safer because alcohol and drugs slow reactions and impair judgment.

text: You are driving in a 70 km/h zone, keeping to the limit. Several vehicles pass you. One of your passengers suggests you should keep up with the other traffic. What should you do?
options: Decide your speed yourself, based on the speed limit and the conditions.
Follow the suggestions and keep up with the traffic.
Speed up to a little bit over the speed limit, because everyone does it.
explanation: Decide your speed yourself, based on the speed limit and the conditions. It helps because higher speeds increase stopping distance and crash severity.

text: You are facing traffic lights (as shown). What do they mean?
options: You may proceed only in the direction of the green arrow.
You must give way to oncoming traffic.
You may proceed only in the direction of the green arrow when the red light has changed to green.

text: You are planning to drive from Darwin to Alice Springs with some friends. To minimize fatigue and make the trip as safe as possible you should
options: Aim to drive for as long as possible when you are feeling good so you can arrive earlier.
Drive during the day, take plenty of breaks and share driving if possible.
Drive mostly at night as there is less traffic on the road and therefore less risk of crashing.

text: While driving, you come across aggressive, selfish or ignorant driving behaviour by another driver. You should -
options: Stay calm and in control of your vehicle at all times.
Respond by using your horn and/or flashing your lights to let the driver know how you feel.
Chase the car to tell the driver how to drive.
explanation: Stay calm and in control of your vehicle at all times. That reduces risk since staying alert and scanning early gives you time to react.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Crossroads ahead, reduce your speed and watch out for other traffic and pedestrians.
Hospital ahead, drive carefully.
Cemetery ahead.
explanation: Crossroads ahead, reduce your speed and watch out for other traffic and pedestrians. It is safer because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: What does this sign tell you?
options: There may be animals on or near the road ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop to avoid collision.
Animals are crossing the road ahead, stop and wait for directions.
You are approaching an animal farm.
explanation: There may be animals on or near the road ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop to avoid collision. It helps because animals are unpredictable and can enter the road suddenly.

text: When reversing, you should -
options: Unbuckle your seat belt so you can reverse as quickly as possible.
Sound your horn to warn other drivers.
Take care and never reverse for a greater distance and time than is necessary.

text: You are in the right hand lane and are planning to go straight ahead through this roundabout. When should you signal left to exit the roundabout?
options: After point O.
After point N.
After point M. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 24 of 121

text: You are driving on a road with a speed limit of 60km/h or less. How much space must you leave when passing a bicycle rider?-
options: at least 1 metre.
at least 1.5 metres.
as much as you think is safe.
explanation: at least 1 metre. It helps because cyclists are vulnerable, and consistent rules keep their movements predictable.

text: If you are going out and going to drink alcohol, the best way to avoid having to drink and drive is to -
options: Organise before hand a way of getting home where you are not the driver.
After you have had a few drinks, start to think about how you will get home.
Wait for one hour after your last drink before you drive home.
explanation: Organise before hand a way of getting home where you are not the driver. It is safer because alcohol and drugs slow reactions and impair judgment.

text: When driving at sunset or dawn on a dark day, what should you do?
options: Turn on your hazard warning lights.
Turn on your lights on low beam.
Keep your sunglasses on to cut down headlight glare.

text: What is meant by this sign on or near a bridge?
options: Slow down and be prepared to give way to vehicles travelling in the opposite direction.
Stop at all times before crossing the bridge and only give way to pedestrians who may be crossing.
Do not overtake a vehicle travelling in the same direction.
explanation: Slow down and be prepared to give way to vehicles travelling in the opposite direction. It helps because giving way prevents conflicts with traffic that has priority.

text: You set out on a fairly long drive to see some friends. After a while you start feeling tired. What should you do?
options: Make sure you get plenty of fresh air circulating inside the car by winding down your window.
Stop at a shop and get a drink that contains caffeine to help keep you awake.
Pull off the road, stop and rest until you no longer feel tired.

text: You should check your mirrors -
options: Before every ride.
Every few seconds so that you always know what is behind you.
Before you accelerate or brake so that you do not force people to change their speed.

text: What is the safest way to stay under the legal alcohol limit?
options: Not drinking any alcohol.
Buying a breathalyser (alcohol measuring instrument).
Exercising and drinking black coffee.

text: At this intersection there are no signs or traffic lights. You are in the car marked A. You want to turn left. What should you do?
options: Enter the intersection and make the turn.
Sound the horn to warn the other driver.
Slow down and give way to car B on your right.

text: If you enter an intersection that is under the control of a traffic controller -
options: Follow the directions of the controller.
Sound your horn at the traffic controller and hope they get out of your way.
Stop at the intersection and then proceed slowly. RUH
explanation: Follow the directions of the controller. It is safer because right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: If you have to downshift for a turn, you should do it -
options: Before you start the turn.
Just as you begin the turn.
While you are in the turn.

text: If the boomgates are down and the signals are flashing at a railway level crossing, you may begin to cross -
options: If you can safely go around the closed gate.
Only when the gate is up and the lights stop flashing.
If you cannot see a train approaching.

text: Overtaking another vehicle requires good concentration and judgement. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: It is best and safest to speed up when a vehicle behind you tries to overtake you.
You need to watch out for all large, long vehicles which are turning.
The faster the vehicle you are overtaking is going, the less distance you need to overtake.

text: If you are stopped by Police while riding a motorcycle on a road or road related area and you are not carrying your rider's licence you could expect to be -
options: Given an on-the-spot fine or summonsed to Court by Police.
Given twelve hours to produce it at your local Police Station.
Told to go home and get it.

text: You are about to emerge from a junction. Your pillion passenger tells you it's clear. When should you rely on their judgment?
options: When the roads are very busy.
When the roads a very quiet.
Never, you should always look for yourself.

text: You are riding in heavy rain when your rear wheel skids as you accelerate. To get control again you must -
options: Change down to a lower gear.
Ease off the throttle.
Brake to reduce speed.

text: You want to make a left turn. You must use your left-hand indicator -
options: At all times.
Only when there is traffic behind you.
Only when arrows are marked on the roadway.
explanation: At all times. It is safer because right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: If you intend to turn left, are you required to give a signal?
options: No, if turning left from a lane marked left turn only.
Yes.
No, if arrows are marked on the roadway. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 89 of 121

text: When riding towards the crest of a hill, it is best to -
options: Slow down and buffer from possible oncoming traffic.
Change to a lower gear and apply more throttle.
Maintain a constant speed so that you do not confuse drivers behind you.

text: The speed limit on this road is 90 km/h. You have just overtaken a vehicle in the left lane. What should you do next?
options: Move into the left lane.
Keep your position in this lane.
Accelerate away from the other vehicle and keep driving in this lane. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 46 of 121

text: When you see older people on or near the road, you should -
options: Slow down and take extra care because they may not see you until you are very close.
Drive around them to keep the traffic moving.
Sound your horn and keep going at the same speed so you do not hold up the traffic.
explanation: Slow down and take extra care because they may not see you until you are very close. That reduces risk since pedestrians are vulnerable and need extra protection.

text: Having a radar detector or jammer in your car is against the law -
options: No matter what your reason is.
Only if it is turned on.
If you purchased it after 1998.
explanation: No matter what your reason is. That reduces risk since detectors encourage speeding and undermine enforcement, increasing crash risk.

text: When you see this sign you should -
options: Come to a complete stop, look both ways for trains and proceed with caution if no trains are approaching.
Slow down, then drive slowly over the crossing looking both ways for trains.
Stop, only if a train is at the crossing.
explanation: Come to a complete stop, look both ways for trains and proceed with caution if no trains are approaching. It is safer because stopping prevents you entering a conflict or hazard unexpectedly.

text: If you see a motorcycle with its indicator on but it does not appear they are turning you should -
options: Be aware that not all motorcycles have self cancelling indicators and the rider may not be aware that it is on.
Sound your horn and flash your lights to get their attention so they can turn off their indicator.
Assume that because the indicator is on they intend to turn. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 64 of 121

text: What will happen if a testing officer asks you for a bribe to pass your driving test and you give it to him or her?
options: Action will be taken against all involved. The penalties are severe and include fines and imprisonment.
Nothing, there is no penalty.
Only the testing officer will be investigated. GENERAL KNOWLEDGE SECTION
explanation: Action will be taken against all involved. The penalties are severe and include fines and imprisonment. It is safer because severe penalties deter dangerous or unethical behavior.

text: The adult passenger in the rear is breaking the law because she is -
options: Not wearing the available seat belt.
Sitting in the back seat.
Distracting the driver.
explanation: Not wearing the available seat belt. It helps because restraints keep occupants in place and reduce injury in a crash.

text: Will a P1 licence be suspended for any speeding offence?
options: Yes.
No.
Only for 10 km/h or more over the speed limit.
explanation: Yes. It helps because licensing rules exist to build experience before taking on more responsibility.

text: Wearing a helmet visor or goggles when riding will -
options: Not make much difference to your riding on a fine day when there is no wind.
Protect your eyes from the wind, dust, rain, insects or stones thrown up by other vehicles.
Reduce your vision and should only be worn in the rain.

text: You are in car A and are going straight ahead through the intersection. Who should give way?
options: Car B.
Whoever gets to the intersection first.
Car A.

text: When riding on a wet or slippery road riders should -
options: Reduce speed so that it requires less time if they need to stop.
Ride at a normal constant speed as sign posted for the area.
Ride around with their hands on the brake lever and foot on the brake pedal in case they have to stop in a hurry.
explanation: Reduce speed so that it requires less time if they need to stop. Lower speed gives you more time and distance to stop on slippery surfaces.

text: When drivers have been drinking, the crashes they are involved in are generally -
options: More serious.
Less serious.
About the same.

text: A turn signal that keeps flashing after a turn is very likely to -
options: Confuse other drivers and cause them to turn into your path.
Damage the electrical system.
Keep other drivers from seeing your brake light.

text: You are riding behind a long vehicle. There is a mini-roundabout ahead. The vehicle is signaling left, but positioned to the right. You should -
options: Keep well back.
Sound your horn.
Flash your headlights.

text: You are driving at night with your headlights on high beam. When should you dip your headlights?
options: When within 200 metres of the vehicle ahead or an oncoming one.
When within 200 metres of an oncoming vehicle only.
Never, you are allowed to drive with your lights on high beam at all times.
explanation: When within 200 metres of the vehicle ahead or an oncoming one. It is safer because reduced visibility means hazards appear later and take longer to react to.

text: What must you do when you are towing a caravan to help other vehicles overtake?
options: Keep at least 60 metres behind heavy vehicles or other vehicles towing caravans.
Drive at least 25 km/h below the speed limit.
Stop immediately and let the faster vehicle overtake.
explanation: Keep at least 60 metres behind heavy vehicles or other vehicles towing caravans. It is safer because extra distance gives you more stopping room and lets others pass safely.

text: You wish to make a right-hand turn from a ONE WAY STREET with no arrows marked on the roadway. You should position your vehicle -
options: On the left-hand side of the street.
In the middle of the street.
On the right-hand side of the street.

text: Speed limit signs (such as the one shown) tell drivers –
options: The minimum speed they are allowed to drive.
The recommended speed they should drive.
The maximum speed they are allowed to drive.

text: When starting to overtake you see the dividing lines ahead change to double unbroken lines. What should you do?
options: Do not overtake because you are not permitted to overtake on double lines.
Continue to overtake because you started when the line was broken.
Keep overtaking and cut in in front of the other car as soon as possible.
explanation: Do not overtake because you are not permitted to overtake on double lines. It is safer because line markings or limited visibility make overtaking unsafe here.

text: When riding towards the crest of a hill, it is best to -
options: Slow down and buffer from possible oncoming traffic.
Maintain a constant speed so that you do not confuse drivers behind you.
Change to a lower gear and apply more throttle.
explanation: Slow down and buffer from possible oncoming traffic. The crest limits your view of oncoming traffic, so slow down and leave space.

text: You are most likely to find this sign -
options: On the approach to a bridge which has room for only two vehicles, slow down and proceed with caution.
When a bridge is not safe to drive on.
If there is a footbridge for pedestrians ahead.
explanation: On the approach to a bridge which has room for only two vehicles, slow down and proceed with caution. This matters because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: You are most likely to find this sign, where -
options: Children may be crossing the road ahead, slow down and be prepared to make a safe stop.
There is an athletic field ahead.
Pedestrians are not allowed.
explanation: Children may be crossing the road ahead, slow down and be prepared to make a safe stop. It is safer because children can be unpredictable and may step out without warning.

text: You buy a car and find that the spare tyre is smooth; the tread is only just visible. If you get a puncture will it be legal to drive the car with a smooth spare tyre?
options: Yes, if the tyre is correctly inflated and the side walls of the tyre are in good condition.
Yes, but you must get the puncture fixed within 24 hours.
No, it's illegal to drive a car with a smooth tyre even if it is the spare.

text: As you approach an intersection with traffic lights, the yellow light turns to red. You must -
options: Stop and wait for the green light.
Speed up to avoid traffic from the left and right.
Sound your horn and proceed through the red light.
explanation: Stop and wait for the green light. That reduces risk since stopping prevents you entering a conflict or hazard unexpectedly.

text: To handle a high speed wobble, firmly grip the handlebars and -
options: Allow the motorcycle to slow down.
Increase your speed.
Quickly apply the brakes.

text: Which statement is true?
options: Pedestrians have no special rights on the roads.
You must give way to pedestrians if there is any danger of hitting them.
You must give way to pedestrians only at marked crossings. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 52 of 121

text: When you see this sign, what must you do?
options: Slow down and be ready to stop and give way to a train.
Stop before the railway crossing, wait for 1 minute and proceed if the crossing is clear.
Drive quickly over the railway crossing.
explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop and give way to a train. That reduces risk since giving way prevents conflicts with traffic that has priority.

text: When overtaking another vehicle you should NOT move back in front of it, unless –
options: The driver of the vehicle signals it is safe to do so.
You can see the overtaken vehicle in your rear vision mirror.
An oncoming car appears over a hill.

text: Do cyclist have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers and motorcycle riders?
options: No, they must give way to cars at all times when riding on the road.
Yes.
No, they must always ride on the footpath. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 7 of 121

text: Are motorists allowed to use a bike lane?
options: No.
Yes, only to enter or leave a side street or to enter or leave a parking space.
Yes, only when travelling in a speed zone of 60km/h or less.

text: You should angle park -
options: Where there are markings or a sign indicating angle park.
Where the road is very wide.
Where there is plenty of room from the centre line. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 97 of 121

text: You are about to move away from the kerb in your car. What is the last thing you should do before you move into traffic?
options: Adjust your seat.
Put on your seat belt.
Complete a shoulder check.

text: You have just passed this sign. Can you park on this road ?
options: No, not at any time.
Yes.
Yes, but only in daylight hours.
explanation: No, not at any time. It helps because parking safely and being visible prevents collisions and obstruction.

text: Are you permitted to make a U-Turn at traffic lights?
options: Yes, at all times.
No unless there is a U-TURN Permitted sign at the intersection.
Yes, if there is no danger of colliding with another vehicle. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 35 of 121

text: You are most likely to find this sign, where –
options: Children may be crossing the road ahead, slow down and be prepared to make a safe stop.
There is an athletic field ahead.
Pedestrians are not allowed. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 73 of 121

text: You set out on a fairly long drive to see some friends. After a while you start feeling tired. What should you do?
options: Pull off the road, stop and rest until you no longer feel tired.
Stop at a shop and get a drink that contains caffeine to help keep you awake.
Make sure you get plenty of fresh air circulating inside the car by winding down your window.
explanation: Pull off the road, stop and rest until you no longer feel tired. It helps because worn tyres lose grip and are illegal, increasing stopping distance and blowout risk.

text: As you approach an intersection with traffic lights, the yellow light turns to red. You must -
options: Stop and wait for the green light.
Sound your horn and proceed through the red light.
Speed up to avoid traffic from the left and right. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 37 of 121

text: A turn signal that keeps flashing after a turn is very likely to -
options: Keep other drivers from seeing your brake light.
Confuse other drivers which may result in an accident.
Damage the electrical system.

text: When riding past parked cars motorcycle riders should -
options: Be ready to sound their horn if someone should open a door or step from between the cars.
Create sufficient space from the cars to avoid opening doors or people stepping from between the cars.
Flash the bike's headlight as a warning to anyone in or near the cars.

text: Overtaking another vehicle requires good concentration and judgement. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: You need to watch out for all large, long vehicles which are turning.
It is best and safest to speed up when a vehicle behind you tries to overtake you.
The faster the vehicle you are overtaking is going, the less distance you need to overtake.
explanation: You need to watch out for all large, long vehicles which are turning. It is safer because overtake only when the road is clear and it is safe for all traffic.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Stop sign ahead, slow down and prepare to stop.
You are approaching a roundabout, prepare to give way.
One way traffic ahead.
explanation: Stop sign ahead, slow down and prepare to stop. It is safer because stopping prevents you entering a conflict or hazard unexpectedly.

text: You are riding along on a sealed road when you see sand on the road ahead. What should you do?
options: Slow down because it takes longer to stop on a slippery road surface.
Stay at the same speed.
Increase your speed.

text: When an oncoming vehicle seems ready to turn across your path as you approach it, you should -
options: Check your mirrors, slow down and, if possible, move to your left away from the vehicle.
Keep your speed and lane position constant so the driver knows you want to go straight ahead.
Increase your speed so you can get clear of the car before it turns.
explanation: Check your mirrors, slow down and, if possible, move to your left away from the vehicle. Slowing and moving left creates space if the vehicle turns across your path.

text: You are most likely to find this sign -
options: If there is a footbridge for pedestrians ahead.
When a bridge is not safe to drive on.
On the approach to a bridge which has room for only two vehicles, slow down and proceed with caution.

text: You wish to go straight ahead at this roundabout. Which statement is true?
options: You must leave the roundabout in the same lane as you entered.
You must enter in the right lane and leave in the left.
You must always leave the roundabout in the left lane.
explanation: You must leave the roundabout in the same lane as you entered. It helps because roundabouts rely on lane discipline and giving way to avoid side impacts.

text: You are driving on a freeway and realise you forgot something at home. You want to go back for it. Can you do a U-turn on this road?
options: No, not at any time.
Yes, any time.
Yes, providing you use the gravel joining roads.
explanation: No, not at any time. This matters because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: What is the safest way to stay under the legal alcohol limit?
options: Not drinking any alcohol.
Buying a breathalyser (alcohol measuring instrument).
Exercising and drinking black coffee.
explanation: Not drinking any alcohol. That reduces risk since alcohol and drugs slow reactions and impair judgment.

text: What does the below traffic light mean?
options: All traffic can proceed through the intersection.
Only buses can proceed through the intersection while all other vehicles stay.
All vehicles must wait for the light to turn green.

text: Having 1 or 2 alcoholic drinks before driving -
options: Has no effect on your driving ability.
Improves your driving ability.
Will affect your reactions and judgement.

text: If elderly people or children are on a pedestrian crossing you will probably need to -
options: Wait extra time to allow them to cross safely.
Sound your horn to hurry them up.
Drive around them so you don't hold up traffic.
explanation: Wait extra time to allow them to cross safely. That reduces risk since children can be unpredictable and may step out without warning.

text: Where do you stop at temporary traffic lights?
options: At the 'Stop here on red signal' sign.
Where the lane ends.
After the traffic lights, but before the construction zone. TRAFFIC SIGNS SECTION
explanation: At the 'Stop here on red signal' sign. It helps because lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: You are driving behind a long vehicle (as shown) which has a sign saying DO NOT OVERTAKE TURNING VEHICLE. The long vehicle indicates that it is going to turn left. You -
options: Must let the long vehicle turn first.
May move to the left-hand side of the road and pass the long vehicle.
May pass the truck because it cannot turn left from the middle lane.
explanation: Must let the long vehicle turn first. It is safer because overtake only when the road is clear and it is safe for all traffic.

text: You are looking for somewhere to park your motorcycle. The area is full EXCEPT for spaces marked 'Disabled Use'. You can -
options: Use these spaces when elsewhere is full.
Park if you stay with your motorcycle.
Not park there.

text: You drive towards these people on the road. What should you do?
options: Slow down until they are half way through the crossing and drive on.
Stop and give way if there is any danger of hitting them.
Continue at the same speed and sound the horn.

text: At night you should -
options: Drive closer to the vehicle in front so they can see you better.
Leave a longer gap between your vehicle and the vehicle in front.
Use your hazard warning lights when overtaking another vehicle.

text: When learning to ride you should -
options: Gain experience in complex traffic situations to build your skills quickly.
Start in quiet streets that you know well.
Ride in groups so that you are protected from cars.

text: When a road is wet the most slippery part is likely to be -
options: The centre of your lane.
The left side of your lane.
The right side of your lane.
explanation: The centre of your lane. Oil and grime build up in the centre, making it the slickest part when wet.

text: To ensure a helmet is in good condition you should -
options: Only purchase a new one. Never buy a second hand helmet.
Only buy a helmet that someone else has tried out first.
Check to make sure it has not been dropped.

text: If you are charged for street racing (hooning), which of these penalties may apply?
options: You will get three demerit points and a large fine.
You will be given a letter of warning and fined.
You will be fined a small amount and get one demerit point. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 116 of 121

text: Is it an offence to obstruct clear vision of your number plates?
options: Yes, at any time.
Yes, but it is legal for a towbar or bicycle rack to cover the rear number plate.
No, you are allowed to cover your number plates if you want to.
explanation: Yes, at any time. It helps because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: Alcohol is a depressant. This means -
options: It slows down how quickly your brain works.
It makes you calm down and think more clearly.
It speeds your brain up so you can work better.

text: You are approaching a hill or curve. You must not cross the centre line to overtake -
options: If you do not have a clear view of any approaching traffic.
If you cannot see clear road ahead for 100 metres.
If you cannot see clear road ahead for 75 metres.
explanation: If you do not have a clear view of any approaching traffic. This matters because overtake only when the road is clear and it is safe for all traffic.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Traffic lights out of order, Police on duty ahead.
School children crossing the road ahead, prepare to stop.
Traffic controller ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 78 of 121

text: Double unbroken dividing lines are marked on a roadway. You may -
options: Cross them to turn into a driveway or property, if it is safe to do so.
Cross them to overtake a car ahead if it is safe to do so.
Cross them to make a U turn.
explanation: Cross them to turn into a driveway or property, if it is safe to do so. This matters because lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: If you are taking several medications and you want to drive, you should -
options: Drive carefully around your local streets to see if you are affected.
Ask your doctor if the combination of drugs will make it dangerous to drive.
Ask your passengers to let you know if you are not driving as well as you should.

text: If you are driving towards a road works zone and a traffic controller displays a stop sign you must -
options: Stop your vehicle and follow the directions of the traffic controller.
Stop and then proceed if you think it is safe.
Slow down and continue through the road works zone.
explanation: Stop your vehicle and follow the directions of the traffic controller. It helps because stopping prevents you entering a conflict or hazard unexpectedly.

text: Pedestrians who are affected by alcohol, are -
options: One of the most common groups involved in road accidents.
Unlikely to walk near the road and do not require your attention.
Less dangerous than sober pedestrians because they are more careful after drinking.

text: You hold an unrestricted licence and are driving at 100 km/h in the country and pass this sign. What should you do?
options: For the next 5 kilometres you must not exceed 60 km/h unless you pass an end farm animal’s speed limit sign.
You can continue to drive at 100 km/h if there are fences to stop farm animals from getting on the road.
Slow down to a speed that will allow you to stop to avoid crashing into animals on the road. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 94 of 121

text: You are in the pink vehicle, you may overtake the vehicle in front -
options: Not at anytime.
On either side.
Only on its right-hand side.

text: Are you permitted to park in the direction of the arrow?
options: Yes, if you are carrying two or more passengers.
No, not at any time.
Yes, provided no taxis are using the area.

text: You should use your right-hand indicator when -
options: You intend to move to the right, at any time.
You intend to slow down.
You are about to stop.
explanation: You intend to move to the right, at any time. It is safer because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: If you are convicted a second time for street or drag racing, which one of the following penalties applies?
options: Your vehicle may be taken away and sold.
You will have to pay for the storage of your vehicle.
You will not be able to register your vehicle again.
explanation: Your vehicle may be taken away and sold. It helps because severe penalties deter dangerous or unethical behavior.

text: You are waiting at an intersection and the lights are red. The traffic lights change to green. You should -
options: Wait until the traffic behind you makes you move.
Cross the intersection as quickly as possible.
Check both sides of the intersection and then proceed.

text: If a STOP or GIVE WAY sign has been knocked down, for example, as the result of an accident, does the line marked across the road have any meaning?
options: Yes, it has the same meaning as the sign itself.
No, but you must give way if turning.
No, you only need to give way to the vehicle on your right.
explanation: Yes, it has the same meaning as the sign itself. That reduces risk since right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: Police officers may check that you are correctly licensed when -
options: You are stopped for Random Breath Testing.
You stop to pay tolls.
Riding on a freeway or motorway.

text: After drinking alcohol you -
options: Will be able to drive the same as you normally can.
Will drive better.
Can misjudge speed (your own and others).

text: In wet weather when it becomes hard for you to see, you should -
options: Turn on your headlights, slow down, and double your following distance behind the vehicle in front.
Turn your headlights on high beam.
Flash your headlights to warn other drivers.
explanation: Turn on your headlights, slow down, and double your following distance behind the vehicle in front. This matters because wet roads reduce grip and increase stopping distance.

text: Other protective options to wear when riding include -
options: Light cotton shirt and pants.
Nylon jacket and pants.
Back protectors to protect your spine.
