text: You borrow a friend's car and find that the position of the driver's seat puts you sitting a long way from the steering wheel and controls. What should you do?
options: Put up with the discomfort; you should not adjust another person's seat.
Ask your friend for a cushion to place behind your back.
Adjust the seat forward so it's right for you.

text: Riders may make themselves more noticeable to car drivers by -
options: Wearing bright, fluorescent or contrasting coloured clothing.
Riding closely behind cars.
Riding to the side of cars at all times.
explanation: Wearing bright, fluorescent or contrasting coloured clothing. Bright, contrasting gear increases visibility and reduces the chance of being missed.

text: What does this sign means?
options: You must stay in or move to the left lane, unless you are overtaking another vehicle.
You must stay in the left lane and must not overtake any vehicles.
You can overtake vehicles only on the left side.
explanation: You must stay in or move to the left lane, unless you are overtaking another vehicle. It helps because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: How should you merge with traffic when entering a busy road?
options: Watch for a gap and increase your speed to safely merge with the traffic.
Slow down and force your way into the traffic.
Stop, then enter the traffic quickly.

text: When passing a cyclist in a speed zone of 60km/h or less, what is the recommended passing distance?
options: 1 metre.
1.5 metres.
Stay as close as possible. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 59 of 121

text: If you have not ridden a particular motorcycle before, you should -
options: Allow extra stopping distance.
Use the rear brake only.
Not go faster than 30 km/h.

text: When riding on a bumpy road -
options: Rise slightly on the footrests so that you can absorb the shock with your knees and elbows.
Keep your normal seating position.
Take your feet off the foot pegs.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: A sharp depression in the road is ahead, be prepared, slow down.
Do not drive with your lights on high beam.
Police station ahead.
explanation: A sharp depression in the road is ahead, be prepared, slow down. It helps because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: On a road with a maximum speed limit of 110 km/h, a learner driver or rider must not drive faster than -
options: 80 km/h.

text: You are turning right from one of two right turn only lanes. How should you use your indicators?
options: Indicate with your right hand signal the same as any other right hand turn.
You should not indicate at all because it might confuse other drivers.
Indicating in this situation is optional. Give a right hand signal if you think it will help other road users.
explanation: Indicate with your right hand signal the same as any other right hand turn. That reduces risk since predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: At traffic lights what is meant when a red light appears?
options: Stop, wait behind the stop line until the lights change to green.
Stop, wait behind the stop line until the lights change to yellow.
Stop, make sure there is no traffic, then drive straight ahead.
explanation: Stop, wait behind the stop line until the lights change to green. It is safer because stopping prevents you entering a conflict or hazard unexpectedly.

text: When you slow down for a stop, you should -
options: Downshift after stopping.
Downshift only if there is traffic ahead of you.
Downshift before stopping.

text: You want to fit a baby restraint to your car. What should you secure the restraint to?
options: Any seat belt in the back or front of the car.
An anchorage point designed for a baby restraint.
Only at the back using the seat belt provided.

text: Bicycle and motorcycle riders have the same rights to use the road as other motor vehicle drivers. They are however, more at risk in traffic because -
options: They are harder to see in traffic and do not have the same protection as drivers.
They are careless and do not obey road rules.
They ride too fast and do not turn their lights on.

text: In this diagram which light is most likely to make the motorcycle more noticeable to the car driver?
options: The right turn indicator.
The tail-light.
The headlight on high beam.
explanation: The right turn indicator. A flashing indicator creates movement and contrast, so drivers notice the bike sooner.

text: You need to stop quickly, you should use -
options: Both brakes together.
The rear brake only.
The front brake only.

text: These markings on the road indicate -
options: Places where pedestrians have special rights.
Places where you can park.
Places where special speed limits apply.
explanation: Places where pedestrians have special rights. It helps because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Railway level crossing with flashing signals ahead, slow down, drive carefully, and be prepared to stop.
Intersection ahead with traffic lights, prepare to stop.
Red light camera in use at traffic lights ahead.

text: You are driving in busy traffic in an 80 km/h zone. It begins to rain lightly. What should you do?
options: Slow down to a speed that suits the conditions better.
Keep going at the same speed because that's how fast the signs tell you to drive.
Pull over and wait till it stops raining.
explanation: Slow down to a speed that suits the conditions better. It is safer because wet roads reduce grip and increase stopping distance.

text: When you see this sign you -
options: Must not stop your vehicle at the kerb during the times shown.
Must not stop here at any time.
May stop at any time to pick up or drop off passengers.
explanation: Must not stop your vehicle at the kerb during the times shown. This matters because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: When overtaking another vehicle you should NOT move back in front of it, unless -
options: You can see the overtaken vehicle in your rear vision mirror.
An oncoming car appears over a hill.
The driver of the vehicle signals it is safe to do so.
explanation: You can see the overtaken vehicle in your rear vision mirror. It helps because overtake only when the road is clear and it is safe for all traffic.

text: What should you be able to see in each mirror fitted to your motorcycle?
options: About half of the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you.
The lane behind.
Your shoulder and the lane behind.

text: If you are driving and it starts to rain, you should -
options: Slow down using the brake gently, since rain and oil may create a slippery surface.
Put your lights on high beam so you can see better.
Put your hazard warning lights on and increase your speed to avoid the rain.
explanation: Slow down using the brake gently, since rain and oil may create a slippery surface. It is safer because wet roads reduce grip and increase stopping distance.

text: Protective clothing should be -
options: Comfortable without being loose.
Very tight so they won't move if you fall off your bike.
Loose to allow air flow to keep you cool in summer.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Slow down and look out for pedestrians crossing the road ahead.
Stop and help aged pedestrians across the road.
Hospital ahead, slow down and proceed with caution.
explanation: Slow down and look out for pedestrians crossing the road ahead. That reduces risk since pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: Before getting out of your vehicle you must -
options: Check your mirrors and blind spots for pedestrians, bicycles or other vehicles.
Check your seatbelt is back in place.
Check your headlights are turned off. ROAD SAFETY SECTION
explanation: Check your mirrors and blind spots for pedestrians, bicycles or other vehicles. That reduces risk since pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: When travelling behind a motorcycle you should -
options: Sound your horn and flash your lights to get them to move out of the way.
Allow for extra space between you and the motorcycle.
Sit as close as possible.

text: When you wish to turn left at a roundabout you indicate -
options: Left from start to finish.
Only if you think it necessary.
Left only after you enter the roundabout.
explanation: Left from start to finish. It helps because roundabouts rely on lane discipline and giving way to avoid side impacts.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: All traffic must turn back at the roundabout.
Slow down, be ready to stop and give way to all vehicles already on the roundabout if there is a danger of a collision.
Stop at all times and give way to all traffic on your right.

text: To make a normal stop, you should use -
options: Both front and rear brakes.
The rear brake only.
The front brake only.

text: You drive towards these people on the road. What should you do?
options: Stop and give way if there is any danger of hitting them.
Continue at the same speed and sound the horn.
Slow down until they are half way through the crossing and drive on.
explanation: Stop and give way if there is any danger of hitting them. It helps because giving way prevents conflicts with traffic that has priority.

text: When you see children on or near the road -
options: You should slow down and be more careful because they may move suddenly.
You should ignore them and pay attention to the rear vision mirror.
You should reduce your speed by 5 km/h. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 56 of 121

text: It is 3 o'clock in the morning. You cannot see any other traffic. You want to turn right. You may -
options: Not turn right while the arrow is red.
Turn right when you have waited one minute.
Turn right if it is safe to do so.
explanation: Not turn right while the arrow is red. It helps because lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: Where there is parallel kerbside parking, are you allowed to double-park alongside a parked vehicle?
options: No, not at any time.
Yes, if delivering goods.
Yes, if not obstructing traffic.
explanation: No, not at any time. That reduces risk since parking safely and being visible prevents collisions and obstruction.

text: You want to turn left at this intersection. There is an edge line that continues through the intersection. Are you permitted to turn here?
options: Yes, you can cross an edge line to turn into or out of a street.
Yes, only if you are in a taxi, hire car, bus or you live in that street.
No, not under any circumstances.

text: How should you give an arm signal to turn left?
options: C.
A.
B.

text: Which one of the following statements is correct? Seat belts -
options: Save lives and prevent injury.
Do not have to be used in the rear seat.
Are not necessary for good drivers.
explanation: Save lives and prevent injury. This matters because restraints keep occupants in place and reduce injury in a crash.

text: You borrow a friend's car and find that the position of the driver's seat puts you sitting a long way from the steering wheel and controls. What should you do?
options: Adjust the seat forward so it's right for you.
Put up with the discomfort; you should not adjust another person's seat.
Ask your friend for a cushion to place behind your back.
explanation: Adjust the seat forward so it's right for you. That reduces risk since predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: When driving near parked vehicles, you should -
options: Check for parked vehicles with turn signals on, or children about to step out.
Stop, if you see a car with its right-hand indicator on.
Sound your horn and flash your headlights to warn drivers not to pull out.
explanation: Check for parked vehicles with turn signals on, or children about to step out. It helps because children can be unpredictable and may step out without warning.

text: A friend lends you a van that has seats for ten passengers. What type of licence do you need to drive this type of vehicle?
options: A car licence.
A heavy rigid vehicle licence.
A small bus licence.
explanation: A car licence. This matters because licensing rules exist to build experience before taking on more responsibility.

text: If you do not obey road work signs you will -
options: Receive a warning letter in the mail.
Not receive any penalty as road work signs are only advisory.
Receive a fine and possible demerit points.

text: When you see this sign you should -
options: Stop, only if a train is at the crossing.
Slow down, then drive slowly over the crossing looking both ways for trains.
Come to a complete stop, look both ways for trains and proceed with caution if no trains are approaching. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 83 of 121

text: Another vehicle is overtaking you on your right. You commit a traffic offence if you -
options: Speed up while the other vehicle is on your right.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down while the other vehicle is on your right.
explanation: Speed up while the other vehicle is on your right. It helps because overtake only when the road is clear and it is safe for all traffic.

text: When cornering on a wet or slippery surface riders should -
options: Reduce the lean angle of the motorcycle so the tyres will grip better.
Sit towards the back of the motorcycle to give more grip to the rear wheel.
Lean as much as normal for the corner only be smoother on the throttle.
explanation: Reduce the lean angle of the motorcycle so the tyres will grip better. Less lean keeps more tyre contact and grip on slippery surfaces.

text: What is the most important reason why you should keep your motorcycle regularly maintained?
options: To keep the machine roadworthy.
To accelerate faster than other traffic.
So the motorcycle can carry a passenger.

text: You want to drive your car but you have a very bad headache. A friend gives you some of their headache tablets to kill the pain. What should you do before you take these tablets?
options: Read the label and confirm they are not prescription drugs and there are no special warnings on the label.
Ask your friend if the tablets have affected them.
Drink a large glass of milk because this reduces the adverse effects of medicines and drugs.
explanation: Read the label and confirm they are not prescription drugs and there are no special warnings on the label. This matters because alcohol and drugs slow reactions and impair judgment.

text: Is it an offence to obstruct clear vision of your number plates?
options: No, you are allowed to cover your number plates if you want to.
Yes.
Yes, but it is legal for a tow bar or bicycle rack to cover the rear number plate.

text: The diagram shows a marked pedestrian crossing at an intersection. There is also a STOP sign at the intersection. You have already stopped for a pedestrian. Must you stop again at the STOP line?
options: Yes, at all times.
No, if the intersection is clear.
Yes, if there is traffic on your right only.

text: These markings on the road indicate -
options: Places where special speed limits apply.
Places where you can park.
Places where pedestrians have special rights.

text: If you have to downshift for a turn, you should do it -
options: Just as you begin the turn.
Before you start the turn.
While you are in the turn.

text: The speed limit on this road is 90 km/h. You have just overtaken a vehicle in the left lane. What should you do next?
options: Move into the left lane.
Keep your position in this lane.
Accelerate away from the other vehicle and keep driving in this lane.
explanation: Move into the left lane. It helps because overtake only when the road is clear and it is safe for all traffic.

text: You are carrying a pillion passenger. When following other traffic, which of the following should you do?
options: Keep further back than you normally would.
Get your passenger to signal for you.
Get your passenger to keep checking behind.

text: Safety tips when driving near a cyclist, choose the correct answer –
options: You are approaching a children’s playground, slow down.
Bicycle riders are not allowed on the road.
Caution, bicycle riders may be using the road.

text: Are you permitted to tow a caravan with a person riding in the caravan?
options: No, not under any circumstances.
Yes, if the person(s) in the caravan are over 12 years of age.
Yes, provided you do not exceed 60 km/h.

text: Are you permitted to park in the direction of the arrow?
options: No, not at any time.
Yes, provided no taxis are using the area.
Yes, if you are carrying two or more passengers.
explanation: No, not at any time. This matters because parking safely and being visible prevents collisions and obstruction.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Give way sign ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop.
Railway level crossing ahead, slow down and look out for trains, be prepared to stop.
Cattle or sheep crossing the road ahead, drive slowly. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 81 of 121

text: When approaching a marked pedestrian crossing and no pedestrians are in sight, you should -
options: Come to a complete stop before the crossing.
Slow down and be ready to make a safe stop.
Go faster, in case a pedestrian steps onto the crossing.

text: A driver behind you signals their intention to overtake your car. What should you do?
options: Keep to the left and let that driver overtake you.
Speed up so that the driver will not have to overtake.
Signal the driver to remain behind you if it is travelling too fast.
explanation: Keep to the left and let that driver overtake you. This matters because overtake only when the road is clear and it is safe for all traffic.

text: If you have a crash whilst wearing your helmet you should -
options: Check to make sure it is not damaged.
If it is scratched or chipped get it repainted.
Replace it.

text: How old must you be to obtain a learner rider licence?
options: 16 years and 9 months of age.
16 years of age.
16 years and 3 months of age.

text: Is it an offence to refuse to take a POLICE breath test?
options: Yes, always.
No, if you say you haven't been drinking alcohol.
No, if you are a learner driver.
explanation: Yes, always. This matters because alcohol and drugs slow reactions and impair judgment.

text: Wearing the right protective clothing when riding can -
options: Greatly reduce injury in the event of a crash.
Make you very hot and reduce your ability to ride.
Make no difference to you when you ride.

text: Generally, if you hear the siren of an emergency vehicle you should -
options: Pull over to the left until the emergency vehicle passes.
Immediately come to a stop.
Let the emergency vehicle pass and follow it closely behind.
explanation: Pull over to the left until the emergency vehicle passes. It helps because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: When should you especially check the engine oil level?
options: When the engine is hot.
Before a long journey.
Early in the morning.

text: When passengers get in the car and do not put their seat belts on, the safest thing to do is -
options: Say nothing because it's the passengers' responsibility to wear their seat belts.
Drive slower than you normally would so the passengers are safe.
Tell them the car has seat belts and they must wear them.

text: You drive up to a corner where you see some loose gravel on the road. You should -
options: Speed up and drive over the gravel as quickly as possible.
Slow down.
Check the mirrors and change lanes. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 101 of 121

text: Which vehicle is parked correctly?
options: Vehicle B.
Vehicle C.
Vehicle A.

text: When displaying L or P plates, how much of the letter must be clearly visible?-
options: Only enough of the letter so it is clear whether it is an L or P.
Most of the letter.
All of the letter L or P.

text: Which movements shown in the diagram can legally be made by the driver of the purple car?
options: O and P only.
P only.
O, P and Q.
explanation: O and P only. It is safer because lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: Where should you look when following a car?
options: To the right-hand side of the car you are following.
At the car's brake lights
Over or through the car you are following as well as watching its brake lights.

text: When driving on a slippery wet road, for example, one covered in early morning dew, your vehicle will -
options: Be easier to steer and handle.
Be heavier to steer.
Take longer and more distance to stop. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 11 of 121

text: The red car wants to turn right and exit the roundabout in the street indicated by an arrow. Is the car positioned in the correct lane to do this?
options: Yes, the car can make the turn only from this lane.
No, the car should enter the roundabout only from the right hand lane.
Yes, the car can make the turn from either the left hand or the right hand lane.

text: You are going to turn right from a one-way street. Where should you be when you start your turn?
options: Any position if it is safe to do so.
Position M. From the middle of the road.
Position R. As close as possible to the right side of the road. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 114 of 121

text: If you are approaching a cyclist riding on the road and you are planning to turn left at an intersection close by, you should -
options: Be patient and wait until the cyclist is clear of the intersection.
Beep your horn and flash your lights to get them to move out of the way.
Speed up and quickly overtake the cyclist before they reach the intersection. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 29 of 121

text: What should you do if you see this sign?
options: Slow down and watch out for loose stones.
Speed up to avoid damage from loose stones.
Visit the windscreen repair shop ahead. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 88 of 121

text: Stop signs or flashing lights at railway crossings should always be obeyed, because -
options: Trains are fast, heavy and cannot stop quickly.
Pedestrians might be crossing.
Car brakes often fail.
explanation: Trains are fast, heavy and cannot stop quickly. It helps because trains cannot stop quickly, so you only proceed when the crossing is clear.

text: What equipment must be fitted to a motorcycle if pillion passengers are to be carried?
options: Separate footrests and a pillion seat.
Heavy duty shock absorbers.
An engine of more than 250ml capacity.

text: Which side mirror is adjusted best?
options: Mirror A.
Mirror B.
Mirror C.
explanation: Mirror A. This matters because proper mirror adjustment reduces blind spots and improves awareness.

text: When driving near pedestrian crossings, intersections, or school crossings, you should always -
options: Move into the left lane.
Keep your eyes on the speedo.
Slow down, watch for pedestrians and be ready to make a safe stop.

text: You are on an open country road with double unbroken dividing lines. There are no side streets and no entrances to properties. Are you allowed to cross the dividing lines?
options: No, not under any circumstances.
Yes, to overtake another vehicle.
Yes, only to overtake a cyclist if it is safe to do so.

text: You are giving an arm signal ready to turn left. Why should you NOT continue with the arm signal while you turn?
options: Because other motorists will think that you are stopping on the corner.
Because you will have less steering control.
Because you might hit a pedestrian on the corner.

text: The most effective device for protecting passengers when in an accident is -
options: Seat belts.
Safety door latches.
Padded instrument panels.
explanation: Seat belts. It helps because restraints keep occupants in place and reduce injury in a crash.

text: Vehicle O is at a STOP sign -
options: Vehicle O must give way only to vehicle R.
All vehicles must give way to vehicle O.
Vehicle O must give way to vehicles P, Q and R.

text: When you see this sign, you should -
options: Drive carefully and watch out for traffic entering from a side-road intersection ahead.
Take care, trucks crossing the road ahead.
Take a break, rest area ahead.
explanation: Drive carefully and watch out for traffic entering from a side-road intersection ahead. It is safer because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: If you are affected by a legal drug, such as a medicine (e.g. cold or allergy tablets) -
options: You may drive only in daylight hours.
You must not drive.
You must have a passenger to help you drive. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 104 of 121

text: At a pedestrian crossing with traffic lights, when the amber light starts ‘flashing’ after the red stop signal, it means –
options: The traffic lights are out of order and pedestrians must not use the crossing.
You may carefully drive through the crossing, if there is no risk of colliding with pedestrians.
The green light is due. Do not proceed until the green light appears.

text: When making a right-hand turn at the intersection shown, you must give way to -
options: An oncoming vehicle going straight ahead or turning left and any vehicle on your right.
A vehicle approaching from your left and intending to turn right.
Only pedestrians.
explanation: An oncoming vehicle going straight ahead or turning left and any vehicle on your right. It is safer because right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: You are travelling behind a bus that pulls up at a bus stop. What should you do?
options: Watch carefully for pedestrians.
Accelerate past the bus sounding your horn.
Pull in closely behind the bus. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 63 of 121

text: When a road is wet the most slippery part is likely to be -
options: The centre of your lane and painted road markings.
The left side of your lane.
The right side of your lane.

text: What should be displayed upon an approved helmet?
options: An Australian Standards sticker.
Bright stickers to make the helmet more visible to vehicle drivers.
A manufacturer's approval and checked by sticker.

text: Are you permitted to drive a car towing more than one trailer?
options: No, not at all.
Yes, if the combined length of vehicle and trailers does not exceed 15 metres.
Yes, provided you have held a licence for two years.
explanation: No, not at all. That reduces risk since extra distance gives you more stopping room and lets others pass safely.

text: What is the first thing to do if you have a blowout?
options: Hold the hand grips tightly. Gradually close the throttle and let the motorcycle slow down.
Brake lightly on the wheel with the good tyre.
Turn quickly off the road.

text: If you have a crash whilst wearing your helmet you should -
options: Replace it.
Check to make sure it is not damaged.
If it is scratched or chipped get it repainted.

text: When you come to an intersection and the road beyond is blocked with vehicles going in the same direction, what should you do?
options: Wait until there is room for you to completely cross the intersection.
Travel into the intersection and wait until traffic ahead moves.
Proceed if there is no traffic on your right.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: You must drive faster than 100 km/h.
The sign applies to truck drivers only, cars can travel at any speed.
You must not drive faster than 100 km/h.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: You must not turn to the right.
You must not turn to the left or the right.
You must not turn to the left. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 67 of 121

text: The diagram shows a priority sign for buses. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Priority applies at all times.
Priority applies when the bus is travelling in a built-up area.
Priority does not apply when the speed limit is 40 Km/h.

text: Which movements shown in the diagram can legally be made by the driver of the purple car?
options: O, P and Q.
P only.
O and P only.

text: To allow yourself time to stop when following another vehicle in dry weather you should stay at least -
options: Three seconds behind the vehicle in front.
Two seconds behind the vehicle in front.
One car length behind the vehicle in front.
explanation: Three seconds behind the vehicle in front. Three seconds gives time to react and stop smoothly if traffic changes.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Slow down and beware of trucks entering from the side.
Trucks must use low gear.
Heavy vehicle checking station ahead.
explanation: Slow down and beware of trucks entering from the side. That reduces risk since signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: You want to fit a baby restraint to your car. What should you secure the restraint to?
options: An anchorage point designed for a baby restraint.
Any seat belt in the back or front of the car.
Only at the back using the seat belt provided.
explanation: An anchorage point designed for a baby restraint. It is safer because restraints keep occupants in place and reduce injury in a crash.

text: You are facing traffic lights (as shown). What do they mean?
options: Buses must stay while all other vehicles proceed through the intersection.
Only buses can proceed through the intersection.
All vehicles can proceed through the intersection. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 41 of 121

text: When taking a left curve you should -
options: Plan to finish in the left part of your lane.
Brake as late as possible to maintain your speed and balance.
Approach on the left to see around the corner.
explanation: Plan to finish in the left part of your lane. Finishing left keeps you away from oncoming traffic and sets up a safe exit.

text: You are travelling in the left lane and wish to turn right at the intersection. You move to the right lane and a driver behind sounds their horn at you. What have you done wrong?
options: Crossed an unbroken lane line.
Driven too slowly.
Changed lanes unnecessarily.
explanation: Crossed an unbroken lane line. This matters because lane discipline keeps traffic flowing and reduces risky weaving.

text: You approach a person crossing the road. You should -
options: Slow down and sound your horn to hurry up the person.
Slow down or stop to avoid hitting the person.
Maintain your speed and swerve around the person. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 54 of 121

text: When you come to an intersection and the road beyond is choked with vehicles going in the same direction, what should you do?
options: Wait until there is room for you to completely cross the intersection.
Proceed if there is no traffic on your right.
Travel into the intersection and wait until traffic ahead moves.
explanation: Wait until there is room for you to completely cross the intersection. It helps because right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: To help prevent fatigue when riding you should -
options: Dress to protect yourself fully from wind, heat, cold and rain and not ride any longer than two hours at a time.
Stop and rest at least every four hours.
Ride in short sleeves shirt with no gloves to allow the wind to keep you awake.

text: You must give way to pedestrians if there is a risk of hitting them. When driving in poor light, you should -
options: Look more carefully for pedestrians because they are hard to see.
Keep your headlights on high beam all the time.
Always drive in the right hand lane so you can be away from pedestrians.

text: Where do you stop at temporary traffic lights?
options: At the ‘Stop here on red signal’ sign.
After the traffic lights, but before the construction zone.
Where the lane ends.

text: You are waiting at an intersection and the lights are red. The traffic lights change to green. You should -
options: Check both sides of the intersection and then proceed.
Cross the intersection as quickly as possible.
Wait until the traffic behind you makes you move.
explanation: Check both sides of the intersection and then proceed. That reduces risk since lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: Which of the following attitudes is most likely to make you a safer driver?
options: When I drive, I have the main responsibility for my safety and the safety of other road users.
It is up to other drivers to avoid crashing into me.
Crashing or not crashing is a matter of luck.
explanation: When I drive, I have the main responsibility for my safety and the safety of other road users. That reduces risk since staying alert and scanning early gives you time to react.

text: To turn back into the same road from which you joined this roundabout you must -
options: Stay in the right lane all the way round.
Use the left lane all the way round.
Move into the left lane to leave the roundabout. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 28 of 121

text: Do motorist need to indicate when passing a cyclist?
options: Yes.
No.
Only when there is traffic coming the other way.

text: Seat belts and child restraints (e.g. baby capsules and child seats) -
options: Are only needed on short trips.
Are only needed on long trips.
Must always be worn properly, and adjusted tightly.

text: As you drive into an intersection, the lights turn to yellow. You should -
options: Brake immediately to a stop.
Continue through the intersection.
Accelerate as hard as you can.

text: Looking at the diagram, which vehicle must give way?
options: Vehicle A.
Vehicle B.
Either vehicle, there is no rule on giving way when merging.

text: Are you permitted to make a U-Turn at traffic lights?
options: No, unless there is a U-TURN PERMITTED sign at the intersection.
Yes, at all times.
Yes, if there is no danger of colliding with another vehicle.
explanation: No, unless there is a U-TURN PERMITTED sign at the intersection. That reduces risk since lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: When you see the headlights flashing on the front of a bus, what should you do?
options: Be careful, there may be children about.
Drive past the bus only while the lights are flashing.
Stop and wait for the lights to stop flashing.
explanation: Be careful, there may be children about. It is safer because children can be unpredictable and may step out without warning.

text: You are at a busy intersection with slow moving traffic and want to go straight ahead. When the traffic lights change to green you should make sure that -
options: You do not hold up the traffic behind you.
You have the car in the right gear.
You do not block the intersection. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 108 of 121

text: If the police suspect you may have been involved in street or drag racing, they may take immediate action. Which one of the following is correct? The police may -
options: Take your vehicle from you and keep it stored for up to 48 hours.
Take your vehicle to the local police station and keep it till the following morning.
Take your vehicle away and sell it at an auction.

text: Where there are double dividing lines, you may park -
options: At least three metres from the dividing lines.
At least two metres from the dividing lines.
One metre from the dividing lines.
explanation: At least three metres from the dividing lines. It helps because parking safely and being visible prevents collisions and obstruction.

text: How should you merge with traffic when entering a freeway?
options: Watch for a gap and merge with the traffic at the speed it is travelling.
Speed up and force your way into the traffic.
Stop, then enter the traffic quickly.
explanation: Watch for a gap and merge with the traffic at the speed it is travelling. It helps because lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: When can a private car travel in a lane marked by this sign?
options: Only within 100 metres of making a turn.
When carrying at least two passengers.
Only to overtake another vehicle.
explanation: Only within 100 metres of making a turn. This matters because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: When driving near parked vehicles, you should -
options: Stop, if you see a car with its right-hand indicator on.
Check for parked vehicles with turn signals on, or children about to step out.
Sound your horn and flash your headlights to warn drivers not to pull out.

text: As a safety measure before starting your engine, you should -
options: Push the motorcycle forward, checking to see the motorcycle is not in gear.
Engage first gear and apply the rear brake.
Engage first gear and apply the front break.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Road may be slippery when wet, slow down and drive carefully.
Sharp turns in the road ahead.
Road under repair, drive carefully.
explanation: Road may be slippery when wet, slow down and drive carefully. That reduces risk since signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: Roadwork signs must be obeyed -
options: At all times.
Only when no other traffic is around.
Only at night time.

text: You are riding the motorcycle shown, what would you need to do to be able to see the car?
options: Look in the mirror.
Turn your head.
Take off your helmet.

text: When turning left at a roundabout you should enter and leave the roundabout -
options: In the left lane.
In the right lane.
In the lane with least traffic.
explanation: In the left lane. This matters because roundabouts rely on lane discipline and giving way to avoid side impacts.

text: These lights mean that you -
options: Can turn left, but not go straight ahead.
Can turn left or go straight ahead.
Can turn left only if a sign 'TURN LEFT AT ANY TIME WITH CARE' is displayed.
explanation: Can turn left, but not go straight ahead. It is safer because lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: After drinking alcohol you could -
options: Misjudge speed (your own and others).
Be able to drive the same as you normally can.
Be able to pay close attention to details in the traffic.
explanation: Misjudge speed (your own and others). This matters because alcohol and drugs slow reactions and impair judgment.

text: As you approach an intersection, you should check for traffic on your left and right -
options: At all times before entering the intersection.
Only when the traffic is heavy.
Only when you approach a stop sign.
explanation: At all times before entering the intersection. It helps because right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: What does this sign tell you?
options: You are approaching an animal farm.
There may be animals on or near the road ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop to avoid collision.
Animals are crossing the road ahead, stop and wait for directions. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 87 of 121

text: You are driving at night and there is no other traffic around you. When can you use your headlights on high beam?
options: Only on roads that do not have street lights.
On any road where the speed limit is above 80 km/h.
On any road, even if there are street lights.

text: Spilt fuel on the road can be very dangerous for you as a motorcyclist. How can this hazard be seen?
options: By a pitted road surface.
By a rainbow pattern on the surface.
By a highly polished surface.

text: When merging onto the freeway from the entrance, you should -
options: Look for a large enough break in the traffic and adjust your speed so as to fit into the traffic flow.
Sound your horn, turn on your indicator lights and move onto the freeway.
Stop and check the traffic behind you on the entrance.
explanation: Look for a large enough break in the traffic and adjust your speed so as to fit into the traffic flow. It helps because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: When is a motorcycle rider allowed to ride without an approved helmet?
options: Never.
When the rider has a medical certificate.
Only during daylight hours.

text: What should you do when approaching traffic lights which change from green to yellow?
options: Speed up to clear the intersection before the lights change to red.
Stop at the stop line unless you are so close that sudden or sharp braking might cause an accident.
Stop, only if a red light camera is in use.

text: Your car registration expires today. You have your car inspected for registration renewal but it fails the inspection. What should you do?
options: After today you must not drive the car until it has been repaired, passed another inspection and registered.
You have seven days to have the car repaired, after which the RTA considers it to be unregistered.
Go to the RTA and ask them to renew your registration and tell them you will soon get the car fixed.
explanation: After today you must not drive the car until it has been repaired, passed another inspection and registered. That reduces risk since unroadworthy or unregistered vehicles are unsafe and illegal to drive.

text: What is this driver doing that is negligent and illegal?
options: Crossing an unbroken line at a curve.
Not signalling to change lanes.
Overtaking on the kerb side.
explanation: Crossing an unbroken line at a curve. It is safer because careless actions create unpredictable conflicts.

text: This sign means you must -
options: Share this road with other people and vehicles and not exceed 10 km/h.
Drive at 10 km/h if there are pedestrians around.
Reduce your speed to what you think is safe but never below 10 km/h.
explanation: Share this road with other people and vehicles and not exceed 10 km/h. That reduces risk since speed limits manage stopping distance and crash severity.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Vehicles must not stop at the kerb, unless picking up goods.
Vehicles are not allowed to stop at the kerb except in a medical emergency.
Vehicles must not stop at the kerb, except if picking up a passenger.

text: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: By law, all occupants of a car (unless exempt) need to be restrained by a properly fitted and adjusted seat belt or a child restraint.
Occupants in a car fitted with airbags are not required to wear a seat belt.
Seat belts and child restraints are only required on short trips.
explanation: By law, all occupants of a car (unless exempt) need to be restrained by a properly fitted and adjusted seat belt or a child restraint. It is safer because children can be unpredictable and may step out without warning.

text: Which movements shown in the diagram can legally be made by the driver of the purple car?
options: O, P and Q.
O and P only.
P only.
explanation: O, P and Q. That reduces risk since lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: When driving in wet weather, you should -
options: Drive in the middle of the road to avoid splashing pedestrians on the footpath.
Stop and help aged pedestrians across the road.
Watch out for pedestrians, who may hurry and take risks.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Traffic travels in each direction.
No turns permitted.
Double lane bridge ahead.
explanation: Traffic travels in each direction. This matters because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: Are cyclist legally entitled to use the road?
options: Yes, bicycle riders have equal rights and responsibilities to share the roads.
No, bicycle riders must always ride on the footpath.
Yes, bicycle riders must give way to motor vehicles at all times when riding on the road.

text: At low speeds, if the rear tyre goes flat what is the first thing you will notice?
options: The rear of the motorcycle will tend to slide from side to side.
The steering will feel heavy.
Your brakes will not work.

text: Where there are double dividing lines, you may park -
options: At least two metres from the dividing lines.
At least three metres from the dividing lines.
One metre from the dividing lines. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 96 of 121

text: When you see this sign you must -
options: Not exceed 40 km/h and keep a special lookout for bicycle riders, pedestrians and children.
Only enter the street if you live in the local zone.
Drive at a speed less than 40 km/h if you are not a resident of the local zone.
explanation: Not exceed 40 km/h and keep a special lookout for bicycle riders, pedestrians and children. That reduces risk since pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: These lights mean that you -
options: Can turn left, but not go straight ahead.
Can turn left or go straight ahead.
Can turn left only if a sign 'TURN LEFT AT ANY TIME WITH CARE' is displayed.

text: When an oncoming vehicle seems ready to turn across your path as you approach it, you should -
options: increase your speed so you can get clear of the car before it turns.
Keep your speed and lane position constant so the driver knows you want to go straight ahead.
Check your mirrors, slow down and, if possible, move to your left away from the vehicle.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Road narrows ahead, slow down and prepare for a change in traffic conditions.
Form one lane of traffic.
Merging traffic, give way to your right.
explanation: Road narrows ahead, slow down and prepare for a change in traffic conditions. It helps because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: You are driving the car in the diagram. You must stop -
options: Only if there is a car on your right or left.
Only if there is danger of a collision with another vehicle.
Even when there is no other traffic.

text: If there are no signs or markings to advise you, can you choose any of these methods of parking?
options: Yes. M, N and O are all legal.
Yes, N is best but M and O are quite legal.
No, only N is correct.

text: When you see an oncoming vehicle you should -
options: Create a buffer between you and the other vehicle.
Always slow down.
Swerve to avoid it, while braking.
explanation: Create a buffer between you and the other vehicle. A buffer gives you time and space if the other vehicle drifts or swerves.

text: What must you do when you are towing a caravan to help other vehicles overtake?
options: Drive at least 25 km/h below the speed limit.
Stop immediately and let the faster vehicle overtake.
Keep at least 200 metres behind heavy vehicles or other vehicles towing caravans.

text: Looking at the diagram, which vehicle must give way?
options: Vehicle B.
Vehicle A.
Either vehicle, there is no rule on giving way when merging.
explanation: Vehicle B. This matters because lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: Even if the signal at a railway level crossing does not indicate that a train is coming, you should -
options: Slow down, be ready to stop and give way if there is danger of collision.
Speed up and cross the tracks quickly.
Stop completely at all times.
explanation: Slow down, be ready to stop and give way if there is danger of collision. It helps because trains cannot stop quickly, so you only proceed when the crossing is clear.

text: Which vehicle in the diagram must give way?
options: Vehicle J.
Vehicle K.
Vehicle L.
explanation: Vehicle J. It is safer because right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: You are approaching an intersection that has a red light camera. The lights turn yellow when you are too close to stop safely. The lights go red as you get to the other side of the intersection. Will you receive a penalty notice?
options: Yes, but a driver is entitled to advise the Police Service and have the case heard by a court.
Possibly, because you were in the intersection when the lights turned red.
No, because the camera only takes a photo if you cross the stop line after the lights turn red.

text: It is important to scan while driving so you can see everything that is happening on the road. What does scanning involve?
options: Looking in the rear and side mirrors continually when driving.
Looking further ahead down the road when driving.
Continually looking ahead, to the sides and using all mirrors when driving.

text: You are in car A and want to turn right at this intersection. Car B facing you is also indicating to turn right. What path should you take?
options: Both pass in front of each other.
Pass behind each other.
Choose either depending on the traffic.
explanation: Both pass in front of each other. This matters because right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: When riding a motorcycle at night you should -
options: Reduce speed even on roads you know well as you cannot see very far ahead at night.
Ride as you normally would in daytime.
Ride at all times with your headlight on high beam to give you better vision.

text: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Pedestrians must cross the road only at marked crossings and intersections.
You must give way to pedestrians if there is a danger of a collision.
You do not have to give way to adults crossing at children's crossings.

text: When you wish to drive straight ahead at a roundabout you may enter from either the left or right lane. As you continue around you should -
options: Keep in the lane you entered the roundabout.
Move into another lane with least traffic.
Change lanes to get through quickly.
explanation: Keep in the lane you entered the roundabout. This matters because lane discipline keeps traffic flowing and reduces risky weaving.

text: Signaling is -
options: Always required before turning or lane changing.
Not required when turning at traffic lights with a green arrow.
Not required when turning at T-intersections. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 33 of 121

text: Recommended additional protection for riders includes -
options: Wearing kidney belts and back protectors.
Wearing water-proof clothing.
Wearing sunglasses under your visor.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: All traffic must travel in the direction of the arrow.
Follow the arrow unless you are turning right.
Road curves to the left ahead.
explanation: All traffic must travel in the direction of the arrow. It is safer because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: At low speeds, if the front tyre goes flat what is the first thing you will notice?
options: The steering will feel heavy.
The motorcycle will tend to slide from side to side.
The motorcycle will lean heavily to one side.

text: What should you do if you have difficulty concentrating when riding?
options: Stop immediately and rest.
Ride without gloves and in a short sleeves shirt to allow the wind on your body to help you concentrate.
Constantly change your speed up and down to help you concentrate on what you are doing.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Vehicles may park in this area for up to ten minutes.
Motorcyclists may park in this area.
Only vehicles displaying a mobility parking authority may park in this area.

text: In the diagram shown you are being followed very closely by another vehicle, you should -
options: Create more space in front of you by slowing down, until it is safe for the other vehicle to pass.
Attempt to get the other vehicle to drop back by giving a hand signal.
Brake hard to force the other vehicle to drop back.
explanation: Create more space in front of you by slowing down, until it is safe for the other vehicle to pass. More space ahead lets you brake smoothly and gives the tailgater room to pass.

text: How should you overtake a pedal cyclist?
options: Sound your horn to warn the cyclist to get off the road.
Drive as close as possible to the cyclist so he or she will move over and let you pass.
The same as you would another car, with safety. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 44 of 121

text: If you hold a learner or provisional licence class what is the Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) limit?
options: Zero.
explanation: Zero. It is safer because alcohol and drugs slow reactions and impair judgment.

text: You are most likely to find this sign -
options: As you approach a winding road, slow down and drive with caution.
If there is a steep hill ahead.
If an unsealed road is ahead.
explanation: As you approach a winding road, slow down and drive with caution. It is safer because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: You are in car A and want to turn right at this intersection. Car B facing you is also indicating to turn right. What path should you take?
options: Choose either depending on the traffic.
Both pass in front of each other.
Pass behind each other. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 111 of 121

text: Are cyclists allowed on the road even when there is an off road bike path adjacent to the road?
options: Yes. Cyclists can choose to cycle on the road, even when there is an adjacent off road path.
No, cyclists must also use the bike path if there is one.
No, cyclists should not use the road. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 61 of 121

text: Before getting out of your vehicle you must -
options: Check your mirrors and blind spots for pedestrians, bicycles or other vehicles.
Check your seatbelt is back in place.
Check your headlights are turned off. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 103 of 121

text: If you have used illegal drugs you -
options: May drive only in light traffic.
Should drink coffee before driving.
Must not drive.

text: You are driving in a 70 km/h zone, keeping to the limit. Several vehicles pass you. One of your passengers suggests you should keep up with the other traffic. What should you do?
options: Follow the suggestions and keep up with the traffic.
Speed up to a little bit over the speed limit, because everyone does it.
Decide your speed yourself, based on the speed limit and the conditions. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 120 of 121

text: Even if you feel unaffected after drinking alcohol, you should -
options: Be aware that your abilities are decreased.
Drive, but avoid using freeways.
Spend more time than usual looking in the mirrors.
explanation: Be aware that your abilities are decreased. This matters because alcohol and drugs slow reactions and impair judgment.

text: If you are caught street or drag racing three times, which one of the following penalties could apply?
options: You will have to pay for the storage of your vehicle.
You will not be able to register your vehicle again.
Your vehicle may be taken away and sold.

text: Correct riding posture -
options: Will make you more visible to other road users.
Is whatever position you are most comfortable in.
Reduces fatigue and improves control.

text: In the diagram shown you are being followed very closely by another vehicle, you should -
options: Brake hard to force the other vehicle to drop back.
Attempt to get the other vehicle to drop back by giving a hand signal.
Create more space in front of you by slowing down, until it is safe for the other vehicle to pass.

text: What should you do if you have difficulty concentrating when riding?
options: Stop immediately and rest.
Ride without gloves and in a short sleeves shirt to allow the wind on your body to help you concentrate.
Constantly change your speed up and down to help you concentrate on what you are doing.

text: You should expect this sign -
options: When a divided road ends and two way traffic is ahead.
If a one way street is ahead.
If a one lane bridge is ahead.
explanation: When a divided road ends and two way traffic is ahead. It is safer because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: When you come across roadworks -
options: You only have to obey the signs during working hours.
You only have to obey the signs when there are workers about.
You must obey the signs that are displayed at all times. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 5 of 121

text: On a single laned road (as shown), you must always overtake another vehicle on its right except when -
options: The other vehicle is going slower than you.
You are travelling at more than 80 km/h.
The other vehicle is turning right. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 42 of 121

text: This bridge has only just enough room for two vehicles. As you come close to it you should -
options: Maintain your speed, keeping to the limit.
Sound your horn to warn the other driver.
Slow down and pay extra attention.

text: What are you required to do if you develop a medical condition that could affect your driving?
options: Hand your licence in at the nearest police station.
Tell your doctor and let him or her notify the MVR.
Once you become aware of the condition you must notify Motor Vehicle Registry.

text: You approach an intersection in busy traffic and want to go straight ahead. The traffic lights turn green. When are you permitted to enter the intersection?
options: Only when there is room for your vehicle on the other side.
Immediately after the traffic lights turn green.
When the vehicle behind signals you to go.
explanation: Only when there is room for your vehicle on the other side. This matters because right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: The most effective device for protecting passengers when in an accident is -
options: Safety door latches.
Padded instrument panels.
Seat belts. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 117 of 121

text: What will happen if you offer a testing officer a bribe to pass your driving test?
options: Action will be taken against you. The penalties are severe and include fines and imprisonment.
Only the testing officer will be investigated.
Nothing, there is no penalty.
explanation: Action will be taken against you. The penalties are severe and include fines and imprisonment. It is safer because severe penalties deter dangerous or unethical behavior.

text: Can drivers cross centre lines when passing a cyclist?
options: No, drivers should speed up and pass the cyclist as quickly as possible.
Yes, only when motorists are passing a cyclist and only when it is safe to do so. This includes crossing over or driving to the right of the dividing line, including double solid lines.
Yes, only when travelling in a speed zone of 60km/h or less.

text: While driving, you come across aggressive, selfish or ignorant driving behaviour by another driver. You should -
options: Stay calm and in control of your vehicle at all times.
Respond by using your horn and/or flashing your lights, to let the driver know how you feel.
Chase the car to tell the driver how to drive.

text: How close can you park to another vehicle when parked parallel to the kerb?
options: You must leave at least 1 metre front and back.
You must leave at least 2 metres from the front only.
You must leave at least 3 metres front and back.
explanation: You must leave at least 1 metre front and back. This matters because parking safely and being visible prevents collisions and obstruction.

At least 50 metres.
At least 20 metres Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 6 of 121

text: When police officers are at intersections giving directions you must -

Drive through the intersection as you normally would.
Wait for the traffic lights to start working again.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Pedestrian crossing ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop.
Overhead footbridge for pedestrians ahead.
Joggers ahead, drive carefully.
explanation: Pedestrian crossing ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop. That reduces risk since pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

options: All four people.
Only the driver.
Only the driver and front seat passenger.
explanation: All four people. This matters because restraints keep occupants in place and reduce injury in a crash.

text: You are driving the car in the diagram. You must stop -
options: Even when there is no other traffic.
Only if there is a car on your right or left.
Only if there is danger of a collision with another vehicle.
explanation: Even when there is no other traffic. That reduces risk since right-of-way rules prevent conflicts at crossing paths.

text: Where there are no speed limit signs, the speed limit is 100 km/h, unless -
options: There are street lights along the road.
The road you are driving on is gravel.
There's an emergency, which mean speed limits don't apply.
explanation: There are street lights along the road. It helps because higher speeds increase stopping distance and crash severity.

text: Which side mirror is adjusted best?
options: Mirror A.
Mirror B.
Mirror C. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 98 of 121

text: Correct riding posture -
options: Reduces fatigue and improves control.
Is whatever position you are most comfortable in.
Will make you more visible to other road users.

text: If you are driving through a road work zone in the left hand lane and you see this sign you should -
options: Merge to the right and give way to other traffic.
Speed up to get in front of any cars traveling in the right hand lane.
Stop and wait for directions.
explanation: Merge to the right and give way to other traffic. This matters because giving way prevents conflicts with traffic that has priority.

text: When driving at sunset or dawn on a dark day, what should you do?
options: Turn on your lights on low beam.
Keep your sunglasses on to cut down headlight glare.
Turn on your hazard warning lights.
explanation: Turn on your lights on low beam. This matters because reduced visibility means hazards appear later and take longer to react to.

text: When turning you should look -
options: In the direction you wish to go.
Down, so you can see the road immediately in front of you.
At traffic coming from behind.
explanation: In the direction you wish to go. Looking where you want to go helps the bike follow that line.

text: Do you have any responsibilities when opening a vehicle door on a roadway?
options: No, there is no regulation to cover this situation.
No, any following traffic must stop if the door interferes with its progress.
Yes, you must not open a door if you are likely to cause danger to road users or impede traffic.

text: When it is very foggy during the day or night and your vehicle has no fog lights, you should -
options: Slow down and use your low beam headlights and hazard warning lights to make your vehicle seen.
Put on your high beam lights.
Follow closer to other vehicles.
explanation: Slow down and use your low beam headlights and hazard warning lights to make your vehicle seen. It is safer because hazards change quickly and require extra caution.

text: You approach an intersection showing a red light and the sign shown. You wish to turn left. You must -
options: Slow down and turn left if it is safe.
Stop and turn left only if it is safe.
Stop and wait for a green light.

text: You want to give a lift to a friend and his four month old baby. Before you do, you need to make sure -
options: You have a baby restraint properly fitted to your vehicle.
You have enough seat belts for all the passengers, including the baby.
Your driver's licence permits you to carry children under the age of twelve months.
explanation: You have a baby restraint properly fitted to your vehicle. It is safer because restraints keep occupants in place and reduce injury in a crash.

text: Any passenger carried on a motorcycle (not in a sidecar) must -
options: Be eight years of age or older.
Be at least six years of age.
Be a holder of a rider licence.

text: You should leave a gap between your vehicle and the one you are following. In good conditions the gap should be -
options: 3 seconds.
1 second.
2 seconds. RUH
explanation: 3 seconds. It is safer because a larger gap gives you time to react and stop safely.

text: If you intend to turn left, are you required to give a signal?
options: Yes, if turn signals are fitted to your vehicle.
No, if turning left from a lane marked left turn only.
No, if arrows are marked on the roadway.
explanation: Yes, if turn signals are fitted to your vehicle. It helps because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: What equipment must be fitted to a motorcycle if pillion passengers are to be carried?
options: An engine of more than 250ml capacity.
Heavy duty shock absorbers.
Separate footrests and a pillion seat.

text: A good riding position should feel comfortable and allow you to -
options: Have fast effective use of the controls without affecting the balance.
Ride faster in all traffic conditions.
Relax more and enjoy your riding.
explanation: Have fast effective use of the controls without affecting the balance. Quick, precise control use without upsetting balance keeps the bike stable.

text: Under good conditions, when driving behind any vehicle, at any speed, you should -
options: Stay at least three seconds behind the vehicle in front of you.
Drive as close to the vehicle in front as possible.
Stay one second behind the vehicle in front of you.
explanation: Stay at least three seconds behind the vehicle in front of you. It helps because higher speeds increase stopping distance and crash severity.

text: Before changing lanes you should -
options: Signal in plenty of time, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for other vehicles.
Speed up so you are going faster than the traffic in the other lane.
Signal for at least two seconds and quickly change lanes.
explanation: Signal in plenty of time, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for other vehicles. It is safer because lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: Your car registration expires today. You have your car inspected for registration renewal but it fails the inspection. What should you do?
options: You have seven days to have the car repaired, after which the Motor Vehicle Registry considers it to be unregistered.
After today you must not drive the car until it has been repaired, passed another inspection and been registered.
Go to the Motor Vehicle Registry and ask them to renew your registration and tell them you will soon get the car fixed. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 93 of 121

text: When you see this sign you should -
options: Stop in the middle of the railway tracks and look both ways for approaching trains.
Continue at the same speed and not look both ways for approaching trains.
Slow down and be prepared to stop if the lights start flashing, warning you of an approaching train. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 84 of 121

text: When driving on a slippery wet road, for example, one covered in early morning dew, your vehicle will -
options: Take longer and further to stop.
Be heavier to steer.
Be easier to steer and handle.
explanation: Take longer and further to stop. This matters because wet roads reduce grip and increase stopping distance.

text: You are driving in busy traffic in an 80 km/h zone. It begins to rain lightly. What should you do?
options: Slow down to a speed that suits the conditions.
Pull over and wait till it stops raining.
Keep going at the same speed because that's how fast the signs tell you to drive.

text: A loose drive chain on a motor cycle could cause -
options: The chain to fall off and possible rear wheel lockup.
The front wheel to wobble.
The brakes to fail.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Road under repair, drive carefully.
Sharp turns in the road ahead.
Road may be slippery when wet, slow down and drive carefully. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 71 of 121

text: You are driving along this road. You hear an ambulance's siren and see the ambulance in your mirror. You should -
options: Turn into a driveway on the right hand side of the road.
Move to the right and make way for the ambulance.
Move to the left and make way for the ambulance. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 99 of 121

text: You are about to move away from the kerb in your car. What is the last thing you should do before you move into traffic?
options: Check over your shoulder.
Adjust your seat.
Put on your seat belt.
explanation: Check over your shoulder. This matters because staying alert and scanning early gives you time to react.

text: What should you do on approaching a railway level crossing displaying a STOP sign?
options: Stop at all times and proceed when safe to do so.
Slow down to 10 km/h, then proceed through the crossing.
Stop, only if a train is at the crossing.
explanation: Stop at all times and proceed when safe to do so. It is safer because trains cannot stop quickly, so you only proceed when the crossing is clear.

text: Consuming even small amounts of alcohol before riding may -
options: Affect your ability to control your motorcycle and make riding dangerous.
Have no effect whatsoever on you.
Help clear your mind by relaxing you.

text: You see a broken yellow line painted on the roadway adjacent to the kerb. What does it mean?
options: Clearway restrictions apply - you must not stop during the clearway hours.
You may at any time, park along this part of the road for 1 hour only.
Bicycle riders must ride along the yellow line.
explanation: Clearway restrictions apply - you must not stop during the clearway hours. It is safer because predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: If you have been convicted for street or drag racing, which of these penalties may apply?
options: You will get three demerit points and a large fine.
You will be given a letter of warning and fined.
You will be fined a small amount and get one demerit point.
explanation: You will get three demerit points and a large fine. This matters because severe penalties deter dangerous or unethical behavior.

text: If there are no lanes marked on the road, you should drive -
options: Anywhere on your side of the road.
Near to the left-hand side of the road.
Along the middle of the road.

text: You hold an unrestricted licence and are driving at 100 km/h in the country and pass this sign. What should you do?
options: Slow down to a speed that will allow you to stop to avoid crashing into farm animals on the road.
You can continue to drive at 100 km/h if there are fences to stop farm animals from getting on the road.
For the next 5 kilometres you must not exceed 60 km/h unless you pass an end farm animals speed limit sign.
explanation: Slow down to a speed that will allow you to stop to avoid crashing into farm animals on the road. That reduces risk since animals are unpredictable and can enter the road suddenly.

text: An important part of observation is -
options: Scanning.
Constantly performing head checks.
Keeping your chin up and look straight at all times.
explanation: Scanning. Scanning keeps you aware of hazards early, not just what is directly ahead.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Crossroads ahead, reduce your speed and watch out for other traffic and pedestrians.
Hospital ahead, drive carefully.
Cemetery ahead.

text: You should expect this sign, if -
options: You are approaching an intersection with traffic lights, be prepared to stop.
You are approaching a school or playground.
A give way sign at an intersection is ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop.

text: When riding over loose gravel or sand, you should -
options: Avoid sudden or quick movements.
Slow down by using the front brake only.
Change up to a higher gear.

text: You should expect this sign, when -
options: A divided road is ahead, prepare for a change in traffic conditions.
A two lane bridge is ahead, slow down and drive carefully.
Freeway conditions are ahead, maximum speed is 100 km/h.
explanation: A divided road is ahead, prepare for a change in traffic conditions. It helps because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: You want to leave your automatic car parked on a street sloping uphill. You should -
options: Park only on flat areas.
Turn the wheels away from the kerb.
Put the handbrake on and put the transmission in "P" (park). Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 95 of 121

text: If you are convicted of driving with a blood alcohol level that is over the limit for your licence, you could lose your driver's licence. You may also -
options: Be sent to prison.
Be restricted to driving an automatic vehicle.
Have a personal speed limit imposed on you.
explanation: Be sent to prison. It is safer because alcohol and drugs slow reactions and impair judgment.

text: When are you allowed to ride a motorcycle on roads in NSW without wearing a helmet?
options: Never.
When you have a doctor's certificate.
When the temperature reaches 32 degrees in summer.

text: Are you permitted to tow a caravan with a person riding in the caravan?
options: No, not under any circumstances.
Yes, provided you do not exceed 60 km/h.
Yes, if the person(s) in the caravan are over 12 years of age.
explanation: No, not under any circumstances. It is safer because extra distance gives you more stopping room and lets others pass safely.

text: The amount of time it take to react and respond to a sudden change in traffic is generally -
options: Three seconds.
Two seconds.
Less than a second.
explanation: Three seconds. It takes a few seconds to see, decide, and react, so you need time in hand.

text: You want to make a left turn. You must use your left-hand indicator -
options: At all times.
Only when there is traffic behind you.
Only when arrows are marked on the roadway.

text: On a wet road what is the safest way to stop?
options: Use the front brake only.
Use the back brake only.
Use both brakes.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: One lane bridge ahead, slow down.
You may travel only in the direction in which the arrow is pointing.
No left turn. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 68 of 121

text: When you are driving on a two-lane road, which lane should you choose?
options: The right lane to avoid slow-moving vehicles.
The left lane unless you are overtaking.
Whichever lane has the least traffic.

text: In a turn you should tell a pillion passenger to -
options: Lean in the same direction as the rider.
Stay upright.
Lean in the opposite direction from the turn.

text: On a wet road how do you make an emergency stop?
options: Apply the front and rear brakes together.
Apply the rear brake only.
Apply the front brake only if the rear wheel begins to slide.

text: Best braking is achieved when a motorcycle is -
options: Upright and travelling in a straight line.
