explanation: You are not to exceed 60 km/h. It is safer because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: If you hear the siren of an emergency vehicle, you must -
options: Take whatever action is necessary (with safety) to make way for the emergency vehicle.
Flash your headlights to warn other drivers.
Increase your speed to avoid the vehicle.
explanation: Take whatever action is necessary (with safety) to make way for the emergency vehicle. This matters because lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: Motorcycles are more difficult to see on the road than cars or trucks. When changing lanes you should?
options: Sound your horn and indicate longer.
Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Speed up and quickly change into the lane.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Slow down, the maximum safe speed around the next curve in the road is 35km/h.
Winding road ahead for next 35 km.
Next main town 35 km to the right.
explanation: Slow down, the maximum safe speed around the next curve in the road is 35km/h. It helps because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: Which one of the following statements is correct? Bicycle riders -
options: Must obey the road rules.
May not travel on heavy traffic roads.
Must ride against the flow of traffic so they can be seen.
explanation: Must obey the road rules. It is safer because cyclists are vulnerable, and consistent rules keep their movements predictable.

text: To progress to a P2 provisional licence, a P1 provisional driver must hold a P1 licence for a minimum period of -
options: 12 months.
18 months.
24 months.
explanation: 12 months. That reduces risk since licensing rules exist to build experience before taking on more responsibility.

text: You are driving on a road with a speed limit above 60km/h. How much space must you leave when passing a bicycle rider?-
options: at least 1 metre.
at least 1.5 metres.
as much as you think is safe.
explanation: at least 1 metre. That reduces risk since cyclists are vulnerable, and consistent rules keep their movements predictable.

text: To stop a motorcycle well, you should always use -
options: Only the rear brake at high speed.
Both brakes together.
Only the front brake at high speed.

text: How should you merge with traffic when entering a motorway?
options: Watch for a gap and increase your speed to safely merge with the traffic.
Slow down and force your way into the traffic.
Stop, then enter the traffic quickly.
explanation: Watch for a gap and increase your speed to safely merge with the traffic. It is safer because lane and signal rules keep traffic predictable.

text: In this roundabout with two lanes, can the marked car turn right?
options: No, not at any time.
Yes, after changing to the right hand lane.
Yes, at any time.

text: Do you have any responsibilities when opening a vehicle door on a roadway?
options: Yes, you must not open a door if you are likely to cause danger to road users or impede traffic.
No, any following traffic must stop if the door interferes with its progress.
No, there is no regulation to cover this situation.
explanation: Yes, you must not open a door if you are likely to cause danger to road users or impede traffic. That reduces risk since predictable, lawful behavior reduces conflicts.

text: You want to drive your car but you have a very bad headache. A friend gives you some of their headache tablets to kill the pain. What should you do before you take these tablets?
options: Ask your friend if the tablets have affected them.
Drink a large glass of milk because this reduces the adverse effects of medicines and drugs.
Read the label and confirm they are not prescription drugs and there are no special warnings on the label.

text: If you are going out and going to drink alcohol, the best way to avoid having to drink and drive is to -
options: Wait for one hour after your last drink before you drive home.
Organise beforehand a way of getting home where you are not the driver.
After you have had a few drinks, start to think about how you will get home.

text: If one or two of your wheels run off the edge of the roadway, you should -
options: Slow down gradually and ease back onto the road.
Increase your speed and drive back on the road.
Slow down quickly by braking hard.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: Double lane bridge ahead.
Traffic travels in each direction.
No turns permitted. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 66 of 121

text: Where there is parallel kerbside parking, are you allowed to double-park alongside a parked vehicle?
options: No, not at any time.
Yes, if delivering goods.
Yes, if not obstructing traffic.

text: Before beginning to overtake another vehicle, you should -
options: Check to see it is safe, change gear if necessary, and signal your intention before moving out.
Signal and slow down so you will have more room to overtake.
Sound your horn, move out and overtake.
explanation: Check to see it is safe, change gear if necessary, and signal your intention before moving out. That reduces risk since overtake only when the road is clear and it is safe for all traffic.

text: To handle a high speed wobble, firmly grip the handlebars and -
options: Allow the motorcycle to slow down.
Increase your speed.
Quickly apply the brakes.

text: You are planning to drive from Sydney to the Gold Coast with some friends. To minimise fatigue and make the trip as safe as possible you should -
options: Drive during the day, take plenty of breaks and share driving if possible.
Drive mostly at night as there is less traffic on the road and therefore less risk of crashing.
Aim to drive for as long as possible when you are feeling good so you can arrive earlier.
explanation: Drive during the day, take plenty of breaks and share driving if possible. This matters because fatigue reduces attention and reaction time.

text: RUH4 When driving in an area where there are many pedestrians (e.g. a bus stop) it is important to -
options: Slow down and watch for an indication that they will enter the road.
Put your headlights on high beam so they can see you better.
Increase your speed to avoid the chance of hitting them.
explanation: Slow down and watch for an indication that they will enter the road. That reduces risk since pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: A friend lends you his car. It is very noisy and blows a lot of smoke. He tells you the vehicle has been given a defect notice but it's still OK to drive it. What should you do?
options: Before you borrow the car check the defect notice to make sure it is legal to drive the car.
Borrow the car, but always drive it 10 Km/h below the speed limit.
Borrow the car but only drive on streets where the car will not be a danger to others.
explanation: Before you borrow the car check the defect notice to make sure it is legal to drive the car. It is safer because unroadworthy or unregistered vehicles are unsafe and illegal to drive.

text: This person is standing on a pedestrian refuge. If he steps out onto your lane you should -
options: Slow down and sound the horn to warn the person to move back.
Give way to the person if there is any danger of colliding.
Maintain your speed so you do not hold up the traffic. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 55 of 121

text: Stop signs or flashing lights at railway crossings should always be obeyed, because -
options: Trains are fast, heavy and cannot stop quickly.
Pedestrians might be crossing.
Car brakes often fail.

text: You are in car marked A. You wish to overtake car marked B. You should -
options: Wait behind car B until it moves into the left lane.
Cross the unbroken single line and overtake.
Cross the line and overtake only if it is safe. RUH
explanation: Wait behind car B until it moves into the left lane. It helps because overtake only when the road is clear and it is safe for all traffic.

text: Properly adjusted mirrors will allow you to see -
options: About half of the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane beside you.
Into the lane beside you.
Only behind you.
explanation: About half of the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane beside you. That view reduces blind spots and lets you monitor traffic behind and beside you.

text: You give a friend and her 12 year old son a lift. Your friend sits in the front and her son gets in the back. The boy does not put his seat belt on. By law, who has to make sure the child wears his seat belt?
options: You do, because you are the driver.
Your friend does because she is the parent.
The child does because it is always the passenger's responsibility.
explanation: You do, because you are the driver. This matters because restraints keep occupants in place and reduce injury in a crash.

text: Which one of the following statements is correct? Bicycle riders -
options: Must ride against the flow of traffic so they can be seen.
May not travel on heavy traffic roads.
Must obey the road rules. Class C Knowledge Test Motor Vehicle Registry January 2021 Page 50 of 121

text: You see these zig-zag markings on the road in front of you. What do they mean?
options: Take care and look out for pedestrians at a crossing.
Look out for animals on the side of the road.
Be careful because the road ahead is slippery.
explanation: Take care and look out for pedestrians at a crossing. It helps because pedestrians are vulnerable and can step into the road unexpectedly.

text: Before taking any drugs and then driving it is most important to -
options: Plan to have some other person with you.
Know what the effects of the drug are.
Have some food in your stomach.

text: A 'low risk' rider -
options: Has good observation, road positioning and hazard perception skills.
Is someone who does not take unnecessary risks.
Is able to react quickly to hazards because they have excellent reflexes.

text: When you see this sign you should -
options: Drive carefully, you are reaching the top of the hill and will not be able to see a safe distance in front of you.
Watch out, the road ahead may be flooded.
Slow down, there is a dangerous curve ahead.
explanation: Drive carefully, you are reaching the top of the hill and will not be able to see a safe distance in front of you. This matters because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: What does this sign mean?
options: You may travel only in the direction in which the arrow is pointing.
No left turn.
One lane bridge ahead, slow down.
explanation: You may travel only in the direction in which the arrow is pointing. It helps because signs warn of hazards and set expectations for all drivers.

text: When drivers have been drinking, the crashes they are involved in are generally -
options: More serious.
Less serious.
About the same.
explanation: More serious. That reduces risk since alcohol and drugs slow reactions and impair judgment.

text: When you see this sign you must -
options: Slow down and be prepared to give way to traffic on your right only.
Slow down and be prepared to stop and give way to all traffic.
Stop and give way to all traffic even if the intersection is clear.

text: Is it an offence to refuse to take a POLICE breath test?
options: No - if you are a learner driver.
No - if you say you haven't been drinking alcohol.
Yes - always.
